articles.title: Micah Parsons calls out Bo Nix and Drake Maye over NFL Top 100 ranking of Jordan Love
articles.summary: The NFL Top 100 list is finally drawing to a close, with the league’s top 10 players now in the process of being revealed. Naturally, there is a lot of conve...
articles.body:
The NFL Top 100 list is finally drawing to a close, with the league's top 10 players now in the process of being revealed.

Naturally, there is a lot of conversation over some of the rankings, with 92 of the Top 100 now named.

Green Bay Packers defender Micah Parsons is no stranger to voicing his thoughts on what is right and wrong in the NFL.

The Top 100 list has proven no different, with the 27-year-old now venting his frustrations over the ranking of his quarterback, Jordan Love .

Bearing in mind that the Packers missed out on the playoffs last season, Love was ranked 72nd, which was four spots lower than he managed the year prior.

As the list narrows down on the best player in the NFL, Parsons has called out some of the quarterbacks to rank higher than Love.

Micah Parsons calls out Bo Nix over NFL Top 100 ranking

Since Love replaced Aaron Rodgers as the starting quarterback in Green Bay , the Packers have been unable to make it past the Divisional Round.

Last season's 9-7-1 record eventually saw the Packers eliminated in the Wild Card Round for the second consecutive year, yet Parsons feels Love should be ranked higher.

"See, no, no, no. I'm pretty sure Bo Nix had more interceptions, and they probably were tied around the same passing touchdowns," said Parsons .

The Denver Broncos quarterback was not the only to receive backlash from Parsons over his ranking, though, with Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff also feeling the heat.

"They had Jared Goff rated higher than Jordan Love. We swept the Detroit Lions last year, and Jordan Love put up 30-plus on one of the top defenses in the NFL. Like, come on, bro," Parsons added.

The irony is that although Love's quarterback rating has increased year on year, the number of touchdowns he has thrown has actually decreased in each of the last three seasons.

Even Super Bowl runner-up Drake Maye could not escape Parsons' wrath, with the Packers defender debating how much better of a season Maye actually had than Love,

"That's because he went to the Super Bowl. He had an amazing year, second MVP, but I don't know if he's 50-plus slots better than he's not."

To say Parsons is clutching at straws is an understatement. For his QB to rank higher than he did this year, Love needs to put more than nine wins on the board and progress deep into the postseason.

Until then, he won't be considered as one of the top guys in the league.

articles.title: C.J. Uzomah holds an interesting stat in Bengals history
articles.summary: From one franchise QB to the next
articles.body:
The Bengals brought back a familiar face this week in C.J. Uzomah to officially retire from the game of football in Cincinnati.

Uzomah was a big-time fan favorite in the Queen City before leaving after the 2021 season to sign with the New York Jets .

During his time as a Bengal, Uzomah had many memorable plays, but he also holds quite an interesting stat that no one else has.

The former Cincinnati tight end caught Andy Dalton 's final touchdown pass as a Bengal and the first touchdown pass thrown by Joe Burrow .

The Dalton-to-Uzomah score occurred in the first quarter during a 33-23 victory over the Cleveland Browns on December 29, 2019. The Burrow-to-Uzomah score occurred during a 35-30 loss to the Browns on September 17, 2020.

So not only did he catch both touchdown passes, he caught both touchdown passes against the same division rival. You just can't make this up.

Uzomah was a big piece of the Bengals' success in 2021, and it is cool to see him back in town talking to guys like Burrow and others during practice.

He will also be the 'Ruler of the Jungle' during the Bengals ' Week 4 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars .

articles.title: Texas A&M junior WR named to USA TODAY's Top 100 CFB player rankings
articles.summary: Texas A&M WR Mario Craver was the only Aggie named to USA TODAY's Top 100 college football player rankings ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
It's fair to say that Texas A&M enters the 2026 season under the radar, no matter how much talent third-year coach Mike Elko has returned and acquired from the transfer portal months after leading the Aggies to the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history . However, after a record 10 players were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, the national perception is that the Aggies will take a step back this fall.

Until the games are played, predictions are meaningless, but they do provide a window into what fans should expect, and with the new nine-game SEC schedule, half of the conference could end the season at 9-3 or 8-4, making the College Football Playoff Committee's job that much harder, knowing that a 9-3 team has yet to make the 12-team field.

Texas A&M 's brutal schedule includes road tests vs. LSU , Missouri , Alabama , South Carolina , and Oklahoma before hosting the Texas Longhorns to end the regular season. On paper, A&M can afford to lose only two of those games while staying undefeated at home, which would mean defeating Texas for the first time in more than a decade.

On both sides of the ball, Texas A&M's roster is chalk full of NFL talent, while redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed returns for his second full starting season, aided by one of the deepest wide receiver rotations in the country, junior Mario Craver , who reeled in 59 receptions for 917 yards and 4 touchdowns after transferring from Mississippi State , was the only Aggie named in USA TODAY's Top 100 college football player rankings.

Coming in at No. 95, writer Austin Curtwright detailed why the elite playmaker made the cut:

"Craver caught 59 passes for 917 yards with four touchdowns last season as a sophomore, but now has the opportunity to be Marcel Reed 's top target after KC Concepcion was drafted in the first round. The former Mississippi State transfer stalled out late in the season but was on pace for a monster campaign through nonconference play, combining for 443 receiving yards and four touchdowns in Texas A&M's three wins to open the season against UTSA, Utah State and Notre Dame. The explosive 5-9 receiver could be in for a huge year with the Aggies, especially if Reed takes a step forward as a passer."

articles.title: Washington Redskins gear is available to fans in the Commanders' team shop at stadium and online
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders are selling throwback jerseys and T-shirts bearing the Redskins name the franchise discarded in 2020 as racist or offensive.
articles.body: The Washington Redskins name and iconic logo that the NFL team in the nation's capital abandoned in 2020 is back in a manner of speaking. It's on full display and for sale in the team's current merchandise shop. Although the gear bearing the Redskins name is rare and limited to a Mitchell & Ness throwback line of T-shirts or jerseys bearing the name of former players who played with the Redskins name and helmet insignia, it is indeed for sale. Anyone can go to the brick-and-mortar store at Northwest Stadium or online and buy, for example, an Art Monk T-shirt bearing the Pro Football Hall Fame receiver's likeness in his old uniform and in his Redskins helmet. TAYLOR HEINICKE RETIRES FROM THE NFL WITH A FAREWELL SALUTE TO THE WASHINGTON REDSKINS The back of that T-shirt is emblazoned with "Washington Redskins" and Monk's career statistics and records. The shirt costs $49.99. For the same price, fans can purchase a Sean Taylor T-Shirt with the likeness of the former safety in his Redskins uniform before he was tragically slain in 2007. Like Monk, Taylor played for the Redskins, not the Washington Commanders. Taylor's retired No. 21 jersey, complete with the Redskins name on the front and a 75th anniversary Washington Redskins patch, is available for $114.99. The interesting thing about this is the franchise is marketing this gear emblazoned with Washington Redskins script and logos as Commanders gear. The jersey, for example, is described as a Sean Taylor Black Washington Commanders Retired Player Name & Number Mesh Top – even though the Commanders nickname does not appear on the jersey. NFL AND CONGRESS DISCUSS RETURN OF THE WASHINGTON REDSKINS LOGO This is what happens when an NFL franchise builds a long and storied history as the Washington Redskins from 1937 to 2019, then decides the Redskins nickname is racist or otherwise offensive under pressure from liberal fans, some Native American groups and sponsors. The Washington Commanders, as they're known now, have vowed never to return to the Redskins nickname. Current owner Josh Harris said in September 2023 that he understands the nostalgia for the former name but that "there was a portion of our fan base that felt disrespected by the former name." So why, if the Redskins name is bothersome, are the Commanders selling Redskins merchandise? And why are they later this season wearing an alternate helmet with a spear piercing the W insignia, much like the old feathered arrow helmet the Redskins wore in the 1960s? The spear that is part of the so-called "Raise Hail" alternate uniform is an obvious reach at Redskins nostalgia. The gear in the team gift shop is being made available to keep the old trademark in commercial use, according to WUSA9 in Washington. "We are required to maintain the marks in commercial usage so that marks remain under franchise control," a club spokesman told the television station. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE A trademark may be deemed abandoned if its use is discontinued with intent not resume use. The Lanham Act says that three consecutive years of nonuse is prima facie evidence of abandonment. The statutory standard also requires "bona fide use … in the ordinary course of trade," rather than merely token sales made solely to reserve rights. That might be a problem for the Commanders because their contention is that these Redskins items are sold on a limited availability. It should be noted that there are Native American groups who believe the Redskins nickname to be indeed racist. But other native individuals, including a Navajo Code Talkers Association leader and a former Blackfeet tribal chairman, have publicly supported retaining the old nickname and the Native-profile logo. Walter "Blackie" Wetzel, a former chairman of the Blackfeet Tribe and former president of the National Congress of American Indians, helped persuade the club in 1972 to replace its "R" helmet logo with the Native chief helmet portrait most associated with the team. In a 2002 interview, Wetzel said: "It made us all so proud to have an Indian on a big-time team. It’s only a small group of radicals who oppose those names. Indians are proud of Indians." articles.title: Rams' Sean McVay reacts to wild college football controversy: 'Feel like I took a freakin' gummy'
articles.summary: Sean McVay said he "can't even comprehend" the college football eligibility chaos as SEC and Big Ten block former NFL players from returning.
articles.body: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay has one way to view the current college football landscape. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright was expected to become the first-ever player to go from an NFL roster back to an NCAA roster on Wednesday. Wright, who was waived by the Cleveland Browns just two days ago, was reportedly set to reunite with his old Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin, at LSU for this upcoming college season. But hours after he cleared waivers, Wright and the rest of the college football world saw the SEC and Big Ten, which will soon be joined by the ACC and Big 12, create new guidelines for eligibility that would prevent players like Wright who have participated in professional sports from reentering college athletics. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE This came after Wright and other players were granted injunctions or temporary restraining orders allowing them to play this upcoming college season. And most of the lawsuits stem from the NCAA’s new guidelines, which give players five years to play five seasons. McVay was asked about the college controversy on Tuesday during his press session at training camp. He didn’t even hear the full question, but his reaction said it all. "Yeah, I can’t even comprehend this stuff," McVay explained. "It’s wild. I don’t know enough about it other than the fact that guys that can be in NFL camps, if it doesn’t go down for them, they can go back college." McVay put it even more bluntly. "I feel like I took a freakin’ gummy," McVay said, per the Los Angeles Times. COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT Under the new policies set by the SEC and Big Ten, any athlete that has signed with a pro team in the NFL, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition. Attorney Ryan Downton, who represents a number of players trying to get back into the college landscape, told OutKick’s Trey Wallace on Tuesday night that they are currently "working on a legal strategy" on how to move forward against both the NCAA and the respective conferences that enacted the new guidelines. "The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," Downton told OutKick-Fox News on Tuesday night. "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level." articles.title: The 2026 NFL Panic Meter: Rating Every Fanbase's Anxiety Level from 1 to 10
articles.summary: Sports fans have never had less patience.
articles.body:
Sports fans have never had less patience.

And who can blame them? In an era when endless entertainment is one swipe away, nobody wants to wait out a multi-year rebuild—unless there's a clear light at the end of the tunnel.

With that in mind, let's check the temperature across the league and set the panic meter for all 32 NFL fanbases heading into the 2026 campaign.

Josh Allen should have many good years ahead at 30, and the Bills are experimenting with a tweaked coaching staff. This remains in check for now but likely shoots up to 9 if they fall short of the Super Bowl again in 2026.

Nobody expects them to contend this year, but I'd bet it's a two-year leash for Malik Willis and the new Miami regime. Panic level doubles in 2027.

There will be some panic if they take a massive step in the wrong direction after a surprise Super Bowl run, but the young core is locked in and the fans can certainly handle a less-than-awesome campaign.

While the fans know Geno Smith isn't leading them to a Super Bowl, there's got to be a sense of urgency as progress is required from a young and talented offensive core and a rebuilt defense. Otherwise, they'll have to endure another regime change in the 2027 offseason.

A talented team that has regularly fallen short is entering desperate times. Throw in that Lamar Jackson's future remains cloudy from a contractual standpoint, and this is as panicked as it gets.

If this team wastes a fourth consecutive season with Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase, the Zac Taylor era likely ends and a major overhaul follows.

The immediate expectations are low, but there has to be some panic regarding the future and uncertainty at quarterback.

This is realistically their last kick at the can in the Aaron Rodgers era, but it's not a full-blown panic because I think a lot of fans realize they have a sub-Super Bowl ceiling barring a miracle from the 42-year-old quarterback.

The defense is awesome and isn't going anywhere, but it appears to be a make-or-break year for the supposed franchise quarterback. If C.J. Stroud can't get it together, panic mode is activated in Houston by the new year.

In a relatively soft division, they've missed the playoffs in five consecutive seasons. Jobs are on the line for Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones.

It would of course be nice if Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence could build on the red-hot conclusion to their first campaign together, but nobody will sound the alarm if there are some growing pains in Year 2.

As with Cleveland and Houston, most of the panic here is focused on what they get out of the quarterback position. Otherwise, the new coaching staff should have room to breathe as they complete their rebuild.

Best Fantasy Football Team Names for Every NFL Franchise

There's certainly an onus on Bo Nix to take another step forward in his third season, but it does appear the Broncos are becoming a perennial contender with more rope than, say, Buffalo or Baltimore. That's simply because they're earlier in the window.

How much is left in this dynasty's tank? What is Patrick Mahomes at this stage in his career? Is Travis Kelce reaching his expiration date? There's a lot to be anxious about, but three recent Super Bowls must take the edge off.

You would like to see promise from a new coaching staff, action from a new franchise quarterback, and progress from a young core. That's it for now, though.

The window is open in Year 7 for Justin Herbert and Year 3 for Jim Harbaugh. There has to be somewhat of a sense of urgency to finally put it together and win a playoff game for the first time in the Herbert era.

No team is under a more intense microscope. They're coming off back-to-back losing seasons, and they still have just two playoff wins in the decade-long Dak Prescott era. That has to change ASAP or Prescott could be out.

It kind of feels like gravy for a fun and intriguing young team that has limited short-term expectations. But if Jaxson Dart and that talented new core don't deliver at all in 2026, panic skyrockets in John Harbaugh's second season.

It helps that they've been to three of the last nine Super Bowls, but they seem to be either Super Bowl or one-and-done. The bar has been set quite high, and now they're trying to bounce back from a disappointing campaign without their longtime No. 1 receiver and with yet another new offensive coordinator.

Year 3 for Jayden Daniels, who could either take off following a sophomore slump or continue to run into problems and spark concerns that his amazing 2024 rookie season was a fluke. This could reach full panic by the holiday season.

They definitely want to see more progress from Caleb Williams under Ben Johnson, but nobody is calling for this to be blown up if they run into some growing pains in a stacked division.

I get the feeling that if it doesn't happen this year, major changes could be coming to a team that is far too talented to have one playoff win in the last two seasons.

I wonder if Micah Parsons' injury takes some of the edge off for a fanbase that may realize it is not a top-tier contender and faces a challenging campaign in a tough division. The coaching staff and the core aren't going anywhere.

Kyler Murray is a low-risk gamble that at least shakes things up for an otherwise talented team. There's breathing room here.

They probably won't wait around for Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. to try to get it right beyond this season, and they don't want to waste too much more of Bijan Robinson's prime. It won't take much for this to shoot up to an 8 or 9.

They did win the division last season, but this is probably a make-or-break year for Bryce Young. The Panthers aren't far from a potential crossroads, which of course causes a decent amount of anxiety.

Tyler Shough has some room to develop in less than perfectly linear fashion. The Saints remain in the tunnel but the light is there and there's little reason to panic right now.

Some might already be resigned to the notion the window has closed in Tampa. But for those clinging to hope that Baker Mayfield and Todd Bowles have some sort of run left in them, this is the do-or-die campaign.

It's a dark tunnel. Not sure you can even panic without any reason for hope. Resignation oughta be prevailing among this fanbase.

The window clearly won't be open for much longer, but does that matter? They won it all a few years ago and this is a team that should provide a lot of entertainment using what feels like house money in 2026.

The anxiety is tied directly to the training room. If yet another season is derailed by injuries, the 49ers could be facing a full rebuild rather than another Super Bowl chase.

You just won the Super Bowl. You're not allowed to panic until 2027.

articles.title: Players Flying Up 2026 Fantasy Football Boards This Preseason
articles.summary: Success in fantasy football is all about finding value—getting players at a position where they outperform their asking price. That can be easier said than done, though, because those values change throughout the summer.
articles.body:
Success in fantasy football is all about finding value—getting players at a position where they outperform their asking price. That can be easier said than done, though, because those values change throughout the summer.

Fantasy-player values are constantly in flux. For established stars, ADP usually shifts only modestly unless injuries intervene. For less-established players, however, values can rise or fall sharply as the regular season approaches.

For some, it's the opportunity created by an injury; for others, it stems from consistently standing out—or disappointing—on the practice field or from a late change of scenery.

This draft season is no different. As August progresses, players ranging from rookies to established veterans are climbing draft boards.

And per the ADP data at Footballguys , here are some of the biggest risers of late.

WR De'Zhaun Stribling, San Francisco 49ers

Even before De'Zhaun Stribling started smoking defenses in preseason games, the hype was growing around the second-round rookie after Ricky Pearsall was lost for the season to a knee injury.

But that hype has grown to the point that Stribling has gone from a late-round dart-throw to being drafted as a weekly starter in fantasy leagues. And every time a teammate like 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy raves about Stribling's summer, that asking price on draft day goes up.

"Obviously really excited about him," Purdy told The Pat McAfee Show . "He's a smart kid. He's come in and learned our offense. He's got strong hands. Great route runner. We're going to have his back this year. It's a long year as a rookie. We get it. But he's shown flashes, and we're all really excited about him."

Stribling has been productive in both preseason games, catching 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards. He is already being penciled in for a meaningful role in the 49ers' offense. With veteran receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. ahead of him on the depth chart, Stribling could have an opportunity for a larger role if injuries create openings during the season.

Some analysts believe Stribling is worth a fifth-round pick on draft day. That's the high end of where he's being selected, but at this point he's not getting past Round 8 and high-end WR4 territory.

RB Mike Washington Jr., Las Vegas Raiders

When Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty went down in practice last week, fantasy managers who have already drafted had palpitations.

It appears those managers avoided a worst-case scenario, as Jeanty has been diagnosed with a sprained ankle .

But there's no word on how severe that sprain is or how long Jeanty may sit—and that has caused Mike Washington Jr.'s draft stock to rise sharply.

As Will Brady wrote for Rotoballer , Washington brings an impressive resume and plus-athleticism to the table, and he has been showing off the latter in the preseason:

"A fourth-round pick out of Arkansas, Washington Jr. recorded 1,296 yards from scrimmage and nine touchdowns on 195 touches across 12 games for the Razorbacks last season. The 23-year-old has been impressive in preseason action so far, recording 119 rushing yards on 15 carries across two games. Las Vegas also has little in the way of proven competition for Washington Jr. in the backfield, although the team could look to bring in a veteran or two if Jeanty is indeed facing an extended absence."

Washington's draft range has widened amid uncertainty about Jeanty's status. He has been selected as early as Round 6 but has also lasted until Round 10.

He has become the ultimate lottery ticket this year. He could be all but worthless if Jeanty returns soon, or he could be a league-winner if Jeanty's injury lingers well into the season.

One thing is for sure: If you roll the dice on a banged-up Jeanty, adding Washington as insurance is an absolute must.

Most of the players experiencing a massive spike in ADP are either youngsters or rookies.

At 34, Allen's best football is arguably behind him: His last 1,000-yard season came in 2023, and he averaged a career-low 9.6 yards per reception in 2025. Still, he drew more than 120 targets with the Chargers last season.

Allen told reporters that he thinks he can still help Daniel Jones and the Colts offense:

"I'm making plays and moving the chains. Being a veteran, somebody can ask questions and look forward to. Daniel's a guy who is getting better every year. I think last year he was on a big roll, and (I'm) trying to come in and be part of that and help him, and be that little safety blanket."

With Alec Pierce's early-season availability seemingly in question, there could be an early path to targets in Indianapolis. The problem is that Allen's skill set (at this point in his career) is similar to both Josh Downs and Tyler Warren: All three pass-catchers thrive in the intermediate game.

Without Pierce to stretch opposing defenses, things could get awfully crowded underneath. And if the trio cannibalizes one another's targets, Allen signing with the Colts could be more of a bane to Warren and especially Downs than a viable fantasy asset in his own right.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Last year at Indiana, Kaelon Black averaged 5.6 yards per carry, topped 1,000 rushing yards and scored 10 touchdowns on the ground.

Despite that success, though, some were still a bit taken aback when the San Francisco 49ers took him in the third round of April's draft.

However, after missing some practice time, Black has steadily impressed on the practice field, drawing praise from Niners offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak after his preseason debut:

"I loved how he ran. He really brought kind of a spark to our offense. He's a guy who you don't have to block it perfect every time. He's going to muscle his way through for five, six yards, but he's got good speed to burst and get some explosive runs. I thought he did a really good job. His first time in NFL action, the moment wasn't too big for him. He didn't blink. He was ready to go. Love his development. Love where he's at, but he needs to keep getting better, too, and stacking days. I think we're going to have a good player on our hands down the road, but he's got to keep pushing himself every day."

With Jordan James sidelined by a rib injury, Black has a legitimate chance to open the season as Christian McCaffrey's primary backup in San Francisco.

McCaffrey's extensive workload and injury history make Black a potentially valuable contingency option.

First things first. You see that ADP change? Ignore it.

Because Kayshon Boutte's days as a draft-day afterthought are done—as evidenced by the 23.5-spot jump Texans wideout Jaylin Noel experienced in the days since it was announced that Jayden Higgins would miss the entire 2026 season with an ACL tear.

That injury spurred the Texans to swing a trade with the New England Patriots for Boutte, who caught 33 passes for 551 yards and six touchdowns a year ago.

The trade is going to send Boutte shooting multiple rounds up draft boards, as he is now ostensibly the No. 2 wideout for Houston.

But Adam Pfeifer of a Fantasy Life cautions that Boutte's new home may not provide a similar boost to his fantasy value unless his role changes:

"We'll see if his deployment changes on a new team, but coming aboard this close to the start of the season makes it difficult and unlikely. Boutte ran go routes a whopping 38.2% of the time with the Patriots last season, easily the highest rate in the NFL. As a result, his 16.7 yards per reception ranked towards the top of the league. If Boutte doesn't see more intermediate and layup looks with the Texans, he's unlikely to surpass boom/bust FLEX status, despite the fact that he has less competition for targets."

Boutte is a reasonable late-round target, particularly in best-ball formats, where managers do not have to predict his highest-scoring weeks.

But he's still a high-variance WR4/5. So don't get too carried away.

When a player's ADP spikes in a big way in August, it's usually due to one of two things. Either that player has become a preseason hype darling, or the guy ahead of him on the depth chart got hurt.

The latter is the case with New York Jets running back Braelon Allen. Breece Hall is nursing a groin injury, and while there is optimism he'll be fit for the season-opener, he's not entering the season with a lot of positive momentum.

Allen, on the other hand, has impressed in camp, and he told reporters that he's eager to go after missing 13 games with a knee injury a week ago:

"This is huge. Obviously with last year being cut short for me, right when I felt like I was getting into a groove and getting my feet under me, it definitely sucked. This year I don't want to think too much about personal goals or anything like that, but just trying to establish myself and earn respect from my teammates and around the league. Prove myself as a workhorse back."

Allen is not as essential a handcuff to Hall as Washington is to Jeanty. The Jets offense may offer less upside than Las Vegas', and Isaiah Davis would likely share backfield work if Hall misses time.

In a recent draft, I selected Hall in Round 2 and later added Allen as insurance.

Were it not for De'Zhaun Stribling, Ja'Kobi Lane of the Baltimore Ravens might well be the biggest preseason hype darling at wide receiver.

The drumbeat has been steady since camp that the third-round pick out of Indiana has been a consistent standout on the practice field—so much so that when Houston went shopping for wide receivers, Rashod Bateman was mentioned as a player who could be dealt.

That deal never came to pass, but that hasn't stopped the hoopla around Lane. Per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic , new Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle compared the 6'4" 200-pounder to former Saints standout Michael Thomas.

"Mike Thomas had these strong hands where he could pull it down in a way, and you threw it in the vicinity, and you felt like he was going to go get it," Doyle said. "There is a lot of that feeling (with Lane). He's a very friendly guy to throw to."

That's notable praise for a rookie, and Lane appears to have a bright future. But his value lies mostly in dynasty formats—at least in 2026.

Even if you believe Lane will usurp Bateman as Baltimore's No. 2 receiver at some point during his rookie season, he would still be the No. 3 option in the passing attack for a team that was dead-last in the league with 422 pass attempts last season.

Expectations need to be tempered this year unless there's an injury ahead of Lane.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: The Best Fantasy Football Team Names for Every NFL Franchise
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is quickly approaching, which means the peak fantasy football draft window is now open. After months of tracking roster moves, reading reports from beat writers and watching preseason action, it's time for the hard part.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is quickly approaching, which means the peak fantasy football draft window is now open. After months of tracking roster moves, reading reports from beat writers and watching preseason action, it's time for the hard part.

We're talking, of course, about coming up with the perfect fantasy football team name—one that every opponent will remember as you run through your dynasty, re-draft or superflex league en route to a championship.

Whether you're looking to intimidate the competition, elicit some chuckles (or eye rolls) with a preposterous pun or simply give a nod to your favorite squad, we have something for you here.

Join us to run through the best 2026 fantasy team names for every NFL franchise.

Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride regularly creates monstrous fantasy performances. He finished last season as TE1 in point-per-reception (PPR) leagues and should again be one of the NFL's top fantasy tight ends, even if the Cardinals spend the season patching together the quarterback position.

Jacoby Brissett is expected to open Week 1 as the starter, but Gardner Minshew II and rookie third-round pick Carson Beck are also in the QB room.

In the late 1990s, famed pitchman Ron Popeil urged consumers to purchase his signature rotisserie oven and "set it and forget it."

Fantasy managers might not want to do the same with Brissett in their fantasy lineup, but he should be a solid early-season streamer after finishing last season as QB16. While the Cardinals aren't expected to make the playoffs this season, their offensive skill-position group—led by returning stars McBride, Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr.—is quite good.

Whether Brissett holds down the starting job or gives way to Minshew or Beck this season, the Arizona offense may run through rookie first-round running back Jeremiyah Love .

Love was a do-it-all playmaker at Notre Dame, and the Cardinals drafted him third overall to be the new face of their franchise. Though he suffered a high-ankle sprain in his preseason debut, Love should be a PPR star if he's close to 100 percent by Week 1.

Between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., the Atlanta Falcons may or may not have a capable starting QB on their roster. What they do have is one of the NFL's most impressive skill-position groups.

The Falcons' offense is led by running back Bijan Robinson, who mustard, er, mustered the second-most PPR points among fantasy RBs last season and who has averaged 1,883 scrimmage yards in his three pro seasons.

This is an appropriate name for Drake London managers, even if you're not overly familiar with The Clash's iconic 1979 album, London Calling . The Falcons' No. 1 receiver has a knack for putting the ball in the end zone with 16 touchdowns over the last two seasons.

Tight end Kyle Pitts topped 1,000 yards as a rookie but failed to replicate his 2021 success before last year's 928-yard, five-touchdown bounce-back campaign. With Kevin Stefanski bringing a TE-heavy scheme to Atlanta, Pitts managers are likely to leave their opponents... not in a good spot.

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is coming off an injury-hampered season that included four missed games and some unusually low production. However, the two-time NFL MVP is regularly among the top fantasy performers when healthy.

Jackson was QB1 two seasons ago and could easily have another marvelous season in 2026.

This one works on a couple of different levels. For starters, it incorporates wide receiver Zay Flowers, who is coming off a 1,211-yard season. Secondly, it plays on the idea that Jackson may now be underrated following a down year.

Jackson fell 67 spots in the NFL Top 100 for the 2026 season, landing at No. 69. He ranked a far more respectable 35th in Bleacher Report's NFL 1000 .

Sometimes, it's best not to mess with a classic. Gordon Lightfoot's The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald , released in 1976, is certainly that. So is this fantasy name, which has followed running back Derrick Henry since early in his career with the Tennessee Titans.

After racking up 3,859 scrimmage yards and 34 touchdowns in two seasons with the Ravens, Henry appears poised to wreck fantasy opponents once again despite being 32 years old.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Josh Allen, who finished last season as QB1, is the Buffalo Bills' biggest fantasy star. He also happens to be the unquestioned centerpiece of Buffalo's offensive game plan. He has a new top target in DJ Moore this season but has traditionally carried an average receiving corps while racking up yards as a runner.

In other words, Allen's offensive role is all-inclusive.

After years of fans calling to "let Russ cook," the Denver Broncos added Russell Wilson and made him the centerpiece of their offense, which backfired spectacularly on them. However, when the Bills have allowed running back James Cook to do his thing, it's generally gone well.

Cook topped 1,900 scrimmage yards last season while finishing as RB6 in PPR leagues.

The addition of Moore is expected to boost a passing attack that ranked 15th in yardage last season despite having one of the game's most prolific quarterbacks. Fans and fantasy managers will be asking Buffalo's new No. 1 receiver for s'more (some more) easy completions, touchdowns and meaningful wins in 2026.

Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker might not be a legitimate fantasy star. He was limited to 11 games last season and finished as WR69.

However, Coker has regularly flashed in Carolina's offense and looms as a terrific potential late-round sleeper. His current ADP is 144.

This name plays off the idea that Coker could give managers a satisfying taste of fantasy production with a relatively light investment.

Bryce Young hasn't quite established himself as Carolina's franchise quarterback yet. However, he's made steady progress over the past few seasons and could be a quality streamer in 2026 if he makes another jump.

Now is the perfect time to buy low on the former Alabama star.

As a rookie, wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan was an instant sensation. He started all 17 games as a rookie and topped 1,000 receiving yards en route to Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

Entering Year 2, McMillan is the unquestioned king (or pharaoh) of Carolina's passing attack.

Whether you view Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams as the real "iceman" or not—George Gervin would certainly like a word—it is an appropriate nickname for a quarterback who delivered seven fourth-quarter comebacks in 2025 (including the postseason).

The Iceman Cometh is the title of a 1939 work by American playwright Eugene O'Neill. While the play's plot has nothing in common with Chicago football, this is an apt name for managers who believe Williams has arrived as a fantasy league-winner.

Chicago traded wide receiver DJ Moore to Buffalo early in the offseason, which should open big opportunities in the Bears' receiving corps. Moore led all Bears wideouts with 682 receiving yards last season.

Second-year receiver Luther Burden III is one receiver who could explode in the wake of Moore's absence. He's been dealing with a groin injury but is highly valued with an ADP of 43.

Third-year wideout Rome Odunze is the other Bears receiver who should benefit from Moore's departure. Burden has been the trendier pick this summer—Odunze's ADP is only 66—but it's worth noting that he led all Chicago pass-catchers in targets last season.

Walking on broken glass isn't fun, but the 1992 hit by Annie Lennox was far more enjoyable. Whether you plan to sing along as Joe Burrow racks up the points or give opponents an idea of how their matchup is about to go, this is an apt nod to the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback.

Let's just hope that Burrow makes it through the season healthy. Otherwise, this could backfire and become a less-flattering made-of-glass pun.

Akin to a luxury sports car that needs regular cleaning, Ja'Marr Chase is a well-oiled machine. He finished last season as WR4 in PPR formats despite playing half the season without Burrow behind center.

If Cincinnati's dynamic duo is healthy for most or all of 2026, Chase managers should be taking their opponents to the cleaners.

Plenty of NFL teams have stripes on their uniforms and helmets. However, none of them are covered in lines of contrasting colors quite like the Bengals.

This is a great name for managers who choose to stack Burrow and Chase or roster multiple stars from an impressive lineup that also includes Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, Andrei Iosivas and Mike Gesicki. While the latter two are low-end streamers at best, Burrow, Chase, Higgins and Brown are all surefire fantasy starters when healthy.

The Cleveland Browns offense was one of the worst in the league last season. However, rookie first-round pick KC Concepcion is expected to bring brighter days to the Browns' passing attack.

The former Texas A&M star is a big play waiting to happen and should allow managers to Get Down with some sleeper value (The Way They Like It).

The arrival of Concepcion and second-round pick Denzel Boston may diminish the fantasy value of second-year tight end Harold Fannin Jr., who was essentially Cleveland's de facto No. 1 receiver last season.

Still, the Bowling Green product was TE6 as a rookie and is unlikely to fall off the proverbial fantasy map.

For much of their incarnation as a 1999 expansion team, the Browns have been affectionately known as the " Factory of Sadness ." If you are or know a Cleveland fan, you understand why.

Of course, fantasy managers aren't looking to emulate the Browns' recent track record. Why not put a positive spin on a name that should be instantly recognizable?

If you're old enough to remember when most music was released on CDs, you also likely remember what a game-changer the CD burner was.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is a game-changer in the truest sense, and he happens to be quite fast. So this is an apt name even if you have no clue what a CD is.

While Lamb has served as Dallas' No. 1 receiver for most of his career, trade acquisition George Pickens was the more productive Cowboys receiver in 2025, in part because Lamb was limited to 14 games.

Despite sharing targets with Lamb, Pickens finished last season as WR5. Let opponents know that with him in your lineup, their chances of winning are slim.

In Robert Zemeckis' 1985 smash-hit film Back to the Future , an eccentric scientist's teenage sidekick goes back in time to reshape the future. The Cowboys only wish they could go back in time to the 1990s, when they were winning championships and were still Super Bowl-relevant.

The Cowboys now hold the NFC's longest title-game drought. They're hoping that by pairing a new-look defense with an offense led by Dak Prescott, who was QB5 in 2025, they can turn back the clock.

Even if you're not too familiar with Sir Mix-a-Lot, you've probably heard his breakout 1992 single "Baby Got Back" a time or two. Even if you haven't watched a ton of Denver Broncos football in recent years, you're probably aware that Denver has been a prime playoff contender ever since it drafted quarterback Bo Nix with the 12th overall pick in 2024.

Nix is coming off a fractured ankle that he suffered in the playoffs, but he finished as last year's QB7 and should be viewed as a quality fantasy starter in 2026.

Both Nix and the Broncos offense overall should be better following the trade acquisition of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.

The former Miami Dolphins speedster will add a new element to Denver's passing attack, and fantasy opponents may be short on answers if he's rostered as your WR2 or flex.

Serious Broncos fans remember the "Orange Crush" defense of the 1970s and 80s. Denver's current defense, which ranked second in yards allowed and third in points allowed last season, hasn't reached icon status yet, but it should be one of the better units in the NFL this season.

This is a solid name for managers who draft Denver's defense/special teams or who have stars like Patrick Surtain II and Nik Bonitto in their IDP lineups.

In October 1987, Whitesnake's "Here I Go Again" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. The song only held the No. 1 spot for a week and remains the band's only No. 1 single.

Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who was RB3 last season, is likely to go No. 1 overall in most fantasy drafts this year. Don't expect that to be a one-time occurrence.

Jared Goff is still widely viewed as a game manager, but he finished last season as QB8 and remains a great option for fantasy managers who opt to draft a quarterback late. He holds an ADP of 128.

Goff's calm demeanor in the pocket is nothing like that of the ill-tempered Queen of Hearts in Lewis Carroll's novel Alice's Adventures in Wonderland . However, this is still a fun name, and you might earn a few extra chuckles by using it in a guillotine league.

Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is regularly among the top wide receivers drafted, for good reason. He's both a high-volume receiver and a big-play threat, and he finished last season as WR3.

If he's in your lineup, you can probably expect a few winning streaks.

"All You Need Is Love" was a 1967 single by The Beatles. Using it as a fantasy name is fitting since fantasy names are often pun-oriented. Though the band is one of the most elite musical groups of all time, The Beatles' name is itself a pun.

Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love hasn't quite reached elite status, but he's been an above-average starter since taking the baton from Aaron Rodgers in 2023. He's also a solid sleeper option who finished as QB15 last season despite missing a pair of games.

No one is going to confuse the hip-hop group Jurassic 5 with The Beatles, but their 2002 track "What's Golden" is undeniably catchy.

The Packers are hoping that 2025 first-year pick Matthew Golden catches on as a high-end receiver in his second season. He had just 29 catches for 361 yards as a rookie, but with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks both no longer in Green Bay, Golden has sleeper appeal in fantasy this year.

Tucker Kraft figures to be a top-tier tight end if healthy in 2026. The Packers are commonly referred to as "The Pack," and cheese is very much a Wisconsin thing.

While the Houston Texans weren't exactly known as an offensive powerhouse in 2025, wide receiver Nico Collins still managed to finish as WR8.

He's Houston's clear-cut No. 1 target, he's a strong second-round draft target, and he's likely to frustrate many a fantasy opponent in 2026.

It's only been a few years since quarterback C.J. Stroud was the Offensive Rookie of the Year and an up-and-coming fantasy star, but it feels like a distant memory. Stroud has regressed over the past two years. He also missed three games last season, and he finished 2025 as QB21.

The Texans are hoping that an improved running game—thanks to the addition of David Montgomery—and another offensive-line revamp can help Stroud return to his 2023 form. If that happens, managers who scoop up Stroud as a sleeper could be poised to run wild on the competition.

Houston is likely to lead with its defense, which ranked first overall in yards allowed and second in points allowed last season. Fantasy managers who grab Houston's defense—led by stars like Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter and Derek Stingley Jr.—will be poised to put the hurt on opponents.

Though he's coming off a torn Achilles, Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones appears healthy and on track to start in Week 1.

A dynamic dual-threat at his best, Jones is capable of outrunning defenses the same way that Harrison Ford's iconic film character outruns boulders.

Receiver Alec Pierce is still rehabbing from offseason ankle surgery. However, last year's WR28 is still a strong flex option with the sort of big-play ability that can poke holes in opposing defenses at any point in the game.

Tyler, the Creator first broke into the spotlight as a member of the hip-hop collective Odd Future nearly 20 years ago. He has since cemented himself as one of the most influential rappers and producers in the music industry.

Colts tight end Tyler Warren broke through as a fantasy star almost immediately as a rookie last season and has since established himself as Indy's most dependable receiving threat. He finished last season as TE4, and he could be even more prolific this year if Jones stays healthy for the entire season.

When it comes to television dynasties, few can hold a candle to Dick Wolf's Law & Order franchise, which has been running since 1990.

Dynasty managers who bet big on Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence back in 2021 haven't experienced the same level of sustained excellence. However, the Clemson product had a breakthrough season in 2025 and finished the year as QB4.

Jakobi Meyers might not be the Jaguars' only hope at wide receiver, but he's been arguably their most reliable target since they acquired him just before last year's trade deadline.

Despite appearing in only nine games for the Jags last season, Meyers finished third on the team with 61 targets.

The Jaguars allowed starting running back Travis Etienne Jr. to depart in free agency because they envision big things for 2025 fourth-round pick Bhayshul Tuten. He's been heavily hyped as a breakout candidate this offseason and is now trending as a top-50 draft pick.

Tuten's sleeper value has already dissipated, but every manager who bought low on the second-year back figures to let you know about it if he does become a fantasy star.

Since Patrick Mahomes took over as the Kansas City Chiefs' starter in 2018, this has been a popular fantasy name.

It's an obvious nod to John Denver's seminal hit "Take Me Home, Country Roads," and while it's an oldie, it's still a goodie.

Travis Kelce is 36 years old, and he may now be more famous for being married to Taylor Swift than for being a Hall of Fame tight end. However, he's still Mahomes' favorite target, which helped him finish last season as TE3.

This team name may not be obvious at first glance, but it's a nod to a line in Warren G and Nate Dogg's 1994 hit "Regulate."

Receiver Rashee Rice appeared in only eight games last year because of a suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy and a late-season concussion. During his time on the field, though, he averaged 6.6 receptions and 71.4 yards per game.

If Rice can play at a similar pace for a full 17-game season, he should treat managers to a ton of fantasy value.

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is dealing with a sprained ankle, though the injury isn't expected to be long-term, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . As long as he's close to 100 percent by Week 1, Jeanty should deliver plenty of wins to fantasy managers in 2026.

The Boise State product played in a bad offense and behind a terrible offensive line in 2025 and still managed to finish as RB11. With an improved line, an upgraded QB room and an offensive coach in Klint Kubiak, Jeanty could be a top-five fantasy back in 2026.

This one's for the IDP managers who are buying stock in Raiders pass-rusher Maxx Crosby this season. He ranked eighth in IDP scoring last season despite being shut down at the end of the year. He'll also be extra motivated after nearly being traded to Baltimore, only to have the deal voided over health concerns.

"I love being told I can't do something, because I'll go to the end of the world to make it happen," Crosby said, per The Athletic's Sam Warren .

The world may not have asked for it, but it received a new He-Man adaptation with this year's Masters of the Universe . While He-Man has the power when grasping his sword, fantasy managers can power up by snagging Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

Bowers had a down year in 2025 due to an injury and an underperforming offense. However, he was TE1 in 2024 and can return to form with solid quarterback play from Kirk Cousins and/or Fernando Mendoza this season.

If there's one word that can best describe Larry David's surreal comedy Curb Your Enthusiasm , it's probably "awkward." Fortunately, managers should find nothing awkward about rostering Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert this season.

Though he battled his own injuries and numerous injuries along the offensive line and in the backfield, Herbert managed to finish last season as QB10. With mad scientist Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator, Herbert has top-five potential entering 2026.

Receiver Ladd McConkey saw a fairly significant dip in 2025 following his 1,149-yard rookie season in 2024. However, it's worth remembering just how hampered the L.A. offense was by injuries—and McConkey was still a top-30 fantasy receiver.

While McConkey won't be jumping over any barrels in 2026, he's a prime candidate to jump back into the fantasy spotlight, particularly with Keenan Allen no longer in L.A.

A pair of ankle injuries limited running back Omarion Hampton to only nine games as a rookie. However, he flashed elite fantasy upside by averaging 3.6 receptions and 82 scrimmage yards per game while scoring five touchdowns.

Theodor Seuss Geisel—better known as Dr. Seuss—and his famous character Sam-I-Am once suggested that a plate of green eggs and ham can be enjoyed in a variety of ways. If Hampton stays healthy in 2026, managers can expect him to rack up fantasy points in his own assortment of ways.

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is the reigning league MVP, and despite rarely scrambling, he finished last season as QB3 in fantasy.

Stafford is likely to see some statistical regression in 2026 since last year's numbers (4,707 yards and 46 TDs) were so gaudy. However, he still has a great chance to outperform his ADP of 117. Managers who draft him in that range will be getting a luxury.

Managers who snap up receiver Puka Nacua early in drafts will have no worries whatsoever as long as the Rams star stays healthy in 2026.

He caught a league-high 129 passes in 2025 and finished as WR1 in both standard and PPR scoring formats.

Cobra Ka i's time as a cultural phenomenon has largely passed. Kyren Williams' time as a fantasy star has not, though.

Los Angeles leaned heavily on Stafford and the passing game last season while also regularly incorporating backup running back Blake Corum into the offensive plan. Yet Williams still finished with a career-high 1,533 scrimmage yards and as RB9 in PPR leagues.

The Miami Dolphins tore down their roster this offseason and are in the early stages of a complete rebuild. It's still unclear who Miami's top pass-catchers will be in 2026 and whether any player outside of running back De'Von Achane will be fantasy-relevant.

What is clear is that Achane should be fantasy gold if he stays healthy all season. He was last year's RB5, and he's going to be the centerpiece of the Dolphins offense in 2026.

While new head coach Jeff Hafley has told reporters that he was joking when he suggested that Achane could see 40-plus touches per game, that number might not be overly exaggerated.

After flashing his dual-threat ability as a spot starter in Green Bay, quarterback Malik Willis is ready to be unleashed as a full-time starter in Miami.

The Dolphins might not have a very talented roster, but if Willis can sustain the level of play he showed with the Packers (134.6 QB rating in three starts), he's going to lead Miami to a few upsets. With an ADP of 150, he's an intriguing sleeper to consider.

Even Dolphins consultant Troy Aikman has admitted that the team isn't expected to be very good this season. However, fantasy managers who draft players like Achane and Willis will be looking to win now, not in 2027 or beyond.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson is coming off a down year due largely to instability at quarterback. However, the four-time Pro Bowler can still fly.

If you go ask Alice, you'll find that with some steadier quarterback play, he can go right back to being a top-five fantasy receiver.

Like Jefferson, tight end T.J. Hockenson was hampered by bad quarterback play in 2025, finishing the season as TE26. Because of this—and a significant knee injury that impacted him in 2024—Hockenson is more of a sleeper than a fantasy star heading into 2026.

With Oktoberfest right around the corner, now is the perfect time to tap a keg, raise a glass and take a flier on Minnesota's top tight end.

Vikings fans are no strangers to having unexpected quarterbacks deliver success. Two years ago, Sam Darnold went from being a placeholder to a Pro Bowler while leading Minnesota to a 14-win season. Back in 2018, backup Case Keenum hooked up with Stefon Diggs to deliver the "Minneapolis Miracle" and put the Vikings in the NFC title game.

Minnesota has a new quarterback in former Pro Bowler Kyler Murray. The hope is that the free-agent addition can both get the Vikings into the playoffs and push them deep into the postseason.

The New England Patriots have themselves a new No. 1 receiver this season after trading for A.J. Brown in June. Brown finished as WR11 in PPR leagues last season but should benefit from a change of scenery and a more creative Josh McDaniels offense.

With Brown now in Boston—or close to it, as Foxborough is about 38 miles away—this is a strong way to mesh New England's newest star and the 1973 Jim Croce classic "Bad, Bad Leroy Brown."

The Mandalorian and Grogu may have disappointed at the box office, but that won't erase Star Wars' status as an everlasting cultural phenomenon.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye might not spark a fandom that lasts for decades. However, he's just entering his prime and will bring his dual-threat powers to fantasy managers in 2026.

It's a bit surprising that the NFL hasn't done more to tie into (or cash in on) last year's runaway streaming hit KPop Demon Hunters—though the fictional band from the film, HUNTR/X, did perform at Netflix's Christmas Day halftime show.

Fans of both the animated film and New England can use this team name to reference Patriots standouts TreVeyon Henderson, DeMario "Pop" Douglas and Hunter Henry.

There's nothing wrong with being a little humble after blowing a fantasy opponent out of the proverbial water, even if it's facetious.

"Aw, shucks. I know I won by 80, but I really did just get lucky."

This one works if you're planning on regularly winning big with New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough.

Wide receiver Chris Olave probably won't be serving up endless salad and breadsticks in 2026. However, last year's WR6 could have unlimited potential if Shough takes the sort of second-year leap that many expect.

New Orleans drafted wideout Jordyn Tyson in the first round to give Shough a strong second option. However, the rookie is expected to miss up to two months with a hamstring injury, meaning Olave should be peppered with targets early and often.

Anyone who has seen Steven Spielberg's 1982 masterpiece E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial remembers one thing clearly: The titular alien really wanted to phone home.

The Saints signed running back Travis Etienne Jr. in free agency, and managers who scoop up last year's RB10 will be hoping for some out-of-this-world fantasy numbers.

New York Giants receiver Malik Nabers was a fantasy darling as a rookie in 2024, but a torn ACL erased most of his 2025 season. He's still working his way back from the injury, but he has been cleared to participate in team drills and is thrilled about it .

There's a very real chance that Nabers is back in time for Week 1, and fantasy managers will love having him available again.

The character Darth Vader was first introduced to the world in the 1977 film Star Wars . (It wasn't originally called A New Hope .) Ever since, he's become arguably the most recognizable villain in media and entertainment history.

If second-year quarterback Jackson Dart can stay healthy and build on his promising rookie campaign, the talented dual-threat quarterback can become the big bad of opposing fantasy managers in 2026.

What does running back Cam Skattebo have in common with the 1988 party game Scattergories? Well, they both start with the letter "S," and both can bring some fun to a Sunday afternoon.

The New York Jets haven't exactly been a fantasy football powerhouse in recent years, but running back Breece Hall has been a steady high-volume performer. He topped 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of the past three seasons.

Hall had his first 1,000-yard rushing season in 2025 and finished as RB19 in PPR leagues.

As the Raiders' starter, Geno Smith finished last season as QB23. He's probably a mid-level streamer at best this season, though he could bounce back with a highly underrated Jets offensive cast.

Managers who take a chance on the Jets' newest starting quarterback can use this team name to rub it in whenever their foes fall to one of fantasy's most discounted signal-callers.

While few are going to mistake the Jets for title contenders in 2026, their offense could be far better than most expect. Hall and Garrett Wilson are established stars, and New York's tackle tandem of Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou is terrific.

The Jets have some new weapons in the fold, too, including pass-catching tight end and first-round draft pick Kenyon Sadiq .

Coming off a 560-yard, eight-touchdown season at Oregon, he has the potential to be fantasy-relevant early. However, he experienced a setback over the summer while recovering from sports hernia surgery, and the Jets are expected to phase him in slowly .

Last season, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley didn't seem to have the same Vibranium-level of indestructibility that he flashed during his 2,284-yard season of 2024. However, he still finished as RB14 in PPR leagues.

This name is a nod to Marvel's Black Panther, one of the most iconic superheroes in comics and film history. Ideally, new Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will help Barkley return to super-powered fantasy production in 2026.

Mannion will also be looking to get more out of quarterback Jalen Hurts, who finished last season tied as QB8.

With a new-look receiving corps, the Eagles may lean into Hurts' scrambling ability early and often while also spreading the ball around in the passing game. Although the Eagles traded A.J. Brown this offseason, they added wideouts Dontayvion Wicks, Marquise Brown and rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon .

Fantasy managers would undoubtedly love to see Hurts finish as a top-three fantasy QB.

This one doesn't need much explanation for Eagles fans. The "Philly Special" was the name of the legendary trick play that helped the franchise win its first Super Bowl.

The Eagles have won a second Lombardi since then, but the aforementioned play was monumental enough to justify a statue outside of Lincoln Financial Field.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was a low-end streamer last season, finishing as QB18. However, he could be much more productive in 2026.

Pittsburgh added a couple of offensive difference-makers this offseason in wideout Michael Pittman Jr. and running back Rico Dowdle. Its identity should also have much more of an offensive lean under new head coach Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers has told reporters that he'll have " zero debate " about retiring after the 2026 season, meaning fans have one last chance to utilize this classic team name.

Fantasy managers don't usually name their squads after kickers, but this one's too fun to ignore. Plus, Chris Boswell is one of the more reliable options in fantasy.

Though the Steelers ranked a modest 15th in scoring last season, Boswell finished as K9.

Some franchises have the sort of storied history that overshadows individual stars. Pittsburgh is one of them. Its "Steel Curtain" of the 1970s is still as closely associated with Steelers football as any modern-era star.

Pittsburgh produced a top-10 fantasy defense last season, but this team name is all about brand recognition. It'll instantly let opponents know where loyalties lie while also telling them that their show is over.

There is no shortage of rock/Brock puns that can be applied to San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy. This one's a reference to the B-52s' 1978 hit "Rock Lobster."

Purdy missed roughly half of last season with a toe injury, but he finished as QB14 in 2024 and QB6 in 2023. He should be valued as a high-end streamer in 2026.

49ers running back Christian McCaffrey should be a top-tier starter this season if he can remain healthy. He finished as RB1 in PPR leagues last season and has an ADP of 4 despite missing some training camp time with " tightness ."

McCaffrey may not favor Adidas in the same way that legendary hip-hop group Run DMC does, but the King of Rocking PPR has shown that he's Tougher Than Leather.

It shouldn't be Tricky to trust McCaffrey if he looks to be at 100 percent entering Week 1.

San Francisco hasn't had the best injury fortune when it comes to their wide receivers in recent seasons, and it has already lost Ricky Pearsall for the season to a PCL injury. However, the 49ers also brought back former standout Deebo Samuel for another run.

Samuel remains a viable dual-threat who finished last season as WR25 in PPR leagues.

Few things in 1990s cinema were as memorable as the first terrifying introduction to Hannibal Lecter in the thriller The Silence of the Lambs .

Few things in 2025 were as frightening as the Seattle Seahawks' pairing of an elite defense with the good version of quarterback Sam Darnold.

The 2018 first-round pick struggled early in his career with the New York Jets, but he largely silenced critics last season en route to a Lombardi Trophy.

Aiding Darnold and the Seahawks throughout the 2025 season was wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The former Buckeyes star had a massive breakout in Year 3, leading the NFL in receiving yards while finishing as WR2 in PPR leagues.

This name pairs Smith-Njigba with the well-known Outkast classic "Ms. Jackson." Is it silly? A bit, but you have the song in your head now, don't you?

This is the perfect name for diehard Seahawks fans looking to pay homage to the franchise's dominant defense of the 2010s.

Last year's championship defense was known as the " Dark Side ," which is a pretty cool fantasy name in its own right. However, the "Legion of Boom," led by Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas and Kam Chancellor, is one of the most well-known units in league history and is more clearly associated with Seattle football.

Baker Mayfield finished as QB12 last season even though he and his skill-position corps battled numerous injuries.

"I'm telling you, Baker was going through a lot," linebacker Lavonte David told The Arena podcast (h/t NFL.com's Kevin Patra ). "Baker had a lot of injuries that you didn't expect a quarterback to play through."

Mayfield was tied for QB3 in 2024. If healthy, he should be poised for a bounce-back season. He's certainly worth targeting as a starter, and his shake-and-bake style of play could lead a few managers to a fantasy championship.

While fantasy managers may not care about rubber ducks the same way a certain Sesame Street character does, they should be happy to have Bucky Irving in their backfield.

Like Mayfield, he battled injuries last season, but he should also be in store for a redemption arc. Irving was RB13 in PPR leagues two years ago.

With Mike Evans now in San Francisco, someone needs to step into the No. 1 receiver role for Tampa. Coming off a 938-yard, six-touchdown season, second-year wideout Emeka Egbuka is the logical candidate.

Managers should be happy to target Egbuka as a strong WR2 this year.

Julius Caesar purportedly penned the phrase "I came, I saw, I conquered" after winning the Battle of Zela in 47 BC.

Managers drafting Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward are hoping that the second-year signal-caller has the sort of breakout campaign that makes quick work of the fantasy competition in 2026.

Forget about the Charles Dickens classic Great Expectations , which you may have been forced to read at some point in school. This name is all about rookie receiver Carnell Tate , who was drafted fourth overall to provide Ward with a true No. 1 target.

The expectation is that Tate will follow in the footsteps of other Ohio State products like Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave, providing a significant boost to the Titans' offense—and to the fantasy managers who roster him.

This is an apt name for managers who happen to have multiple Tennessee stars on their fantasy roster.

The " Music City Miracle " is almost unquestionably the most famous play in franchise history. Miracle Whip, meanwhile, is the sweeter, tangier cousin of mayonnaise.

While there's certainly room for a Will Levis mayo joke in here somewhere, the general hope is that you'll have a roster that delivers a sweet, tangy and satisfying fantasy experience.

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels battled multiple injuries in 2025. The previous year, though, the then-rookie helped deliver four game-winning drives and six one-score victories while finishing as QB5 in fantasy.

Should Daniels remain healthy in 2026 and regain his rookie form, his managers are likely to steal more than a few victories.

Daniels' impressive rookie performance also boosted star wide receiver Terry McLaurin, who finished as WR7 in PPR leagues in 2024.

While McLaurin isn't known for his pure speed in quite the same way that the McLaren Formula One racing team is—he did run an impressive 4.35-second 40-yard dash at the scouting combine—he is Washington's top big-play threat.

Longtime Washington fans may want to honor the franchise's heyday in the 1980s and early 1990s—a stretch that included three Super Bowl victories. One well-known aspect of that era was the team's powerful offensive line, known as "The Hogs."

While "The Hogs" could serve as a fantasy name in its own right, managers who want to show who is the boss of their league by referencing the 1972 masterpiece The Godfather , based on the 1969 novel of the same name by Mario Puzo.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Flex Rankings, Team Names and More Draft Cheat Sheets
articles.summary: We're two weeks into the NFL preseason, which means that the 2026–27 season is gloriously close. And for fantasy football managers, that means time to prep for the draft is quickly running out.
articles.body:
We're two weeks into the NFL preseason, which means that the 2026–27 season is gloriously close. And for fantasy football managers, that means time to prep for the draft is quickly running out.

While any number of outcomes could happen by the roster-cut deadline on Sunday, August 30, two preseason games in, we have a better understanding of which players are edging out others in position battles and who are early round redraft candidates versus sleepers.

To prepare you for your draft, we'll take a look at flex player rankings in particular, which will help you sort out not only your flex spot but, of course, your bench as well. As a bonus, you'll also find some name inspiration as well as other fantasy draft tips.

Rankings are courtesy of FantasyPros , current as of midnight on August 25, and assume PPR scoring.

It's worth noting that of the 50 top-ranked flex players, 27 are wide receivers, compared to 19 running backs and four tight ends.

Five teams have the highest representation among the top 50 flex players, with three players each landing in the rankings. Put another way, 30% of the top flex players come from just five teams: the Bengals (Ja'Marr Chase, Chase Brown, Tee Higgins), Lions (Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams), Rams (Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams, Davante Adams), Cowboys (CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Javonte Williams) and Bears (Colston Loveland, Luther Burden III, D'Andre Swift).

Bye weeks, accordingly, could get tricky. Of the top 10 players, four have a Week 6 bye, while three have a Week 11 bye. If you can plan ahead with some starter-quality backups waiting on your bench, you'll have an advantage in those weeks when your competitors may be wiped out.

Unless you're in a dynasty league, the only rookie you're likely contemplating in the top 50 is Arizona's Jeremiyah Love. If you are in a dynasty or keeper league, you may also be thinking about Tennessee wideout Carnell Tate, New Orleans receiver Jordyn Tyson or Philadelphia pass-catcher Makai Lemon.

articles.title: How Travis Kelce spends his millions: Inside the Chiefs star's luxury car collection and growing fortune
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce earns around $17 million a year from the Kansas City Chiefs alone. Add endorsement deals, his New Heights podcast, and a very public rela.
articles.body: Travis Kelce earns around $17 million a year from the Kansas City Chiefs alone. Add endorsement deals, his New Heights podcast, and a very public relationship with Taylor Swift, and you're looking at one of the most commercially visible athletes in American sports. Some of that money goes into real estate. A chunk of it, though, goes straight into a garage that reads like a wish list from someone who genuinely loves cars. From a $400,000 Rolls-Royce Ghost to a battered 1970 Chevelle with a V8 he once described as sounding "mean," Kelce's collection tells you a lot about who he is off the field.What is Travis Kelce's most expensive car?The crown jewel is his Rolls-Royce Ghost, a black sedan worth roughly $400,000. Kelce was first publicly spotted in it during a Kansas City Chiefs red carpet event in August 2025. The Ghost is not a car you buy to get somewhere faster. It exists entirely as a statement, and at that price point, the statement is loud even when the ride is whisper quiet.Close behind it sits his 2014 Aston Martin Vanquish, valued at around $300,000. Kelce saves this one for special occasions, and it is reportedly one of his personal favorites in the garage. The Vanquish runs a naturally aspirated 5.9-liter V12 producing 565 horsepower, enough to sprint from 0 to 60 mph in roughly 4 seconds and push past 183 mph at the top end. It is a grand tourer in the truest sense.Does Travis Kelce own multiple Aston Martins?He does. Alongside the Vanquish, Kelce owns an Aston Martin Vantage, believed to be the 2018 model. The Vantage ditches the old naturally aspirated V12 for a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 sourced from Mercedes-AMG, capable of pushing close to 200 mph. It is a sharper, more aggressive car than the Vanquish. Two Astons in the same garage is a deliberate choice, not a coincidence.What classic car does Travis Kelce drive?This one might be the most interesting car in the entire collection. Kelce owns a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle SS convertible painted a deep maroon, modified with dark-chrome detailing, aftermarket wheels, and updated headlights. He has been photographed driving it with Taylor Swift in the passenger seat. On his New Heights podcast, he described the sound of the V8 engine simply as "mean."The original Chevelle SS came with V8 engine options ranging from a 6.6-liter to a 7.4-liter unit producing up to 330 horsepower. It is the kind of American muscle car that predates his NFL career by more than four decades. There is also a related story worth noting: Kelce's 87 and Running Foundation supported a three-year project in which 81 students from the nonprofit Kansas City Operation Breakthrough restored and converted a 1969 Chevelle into an electric vehicle using a Tesla drive unit and an 87-kWh battery pack. The finished car was raffled off to raise funds for the organization.What SUVs and Trucks does Travis Kelce own?Not everything in Kelce's garage is built for a red carpet. He owns a 2020 Mercedes-AMG G63, the flagship version of the legendary G-Class, worth around $180,000. It packs a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 with 577 horsepower and gets from 0 to 60 mph in 4.5 seconds. He also has a GMC Hummer EV pickup, the kind of vehicle you drive through a Kansas City snowstorm on the way to practice, which is exactly what cameras caught him doing.A 2016 Land Rover Range Rover SVAutobiography rounds out the British luxury contingent. Beyond that, Kelce has a Cadillac Escalade, a 2021 Ford F-150 Raptor spotted as recently as early 2024, a 2018 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 from the C7 generation, a 2019 Bentley Continental GT, and a 2017 Genesis G80 he received after being named Pro Bowl MVP in January 2017. There is also a 2014 GMC Terrain Denali that he appears to use most for everyday driving, which, given everything else in that garage, is a detail worth noting.What car did Travis Kelce's brother give him?Travis Kelce still holds on to a 2013 Ford F-150 his brother gave him in his early twenties. The truck was stolen outside a Cleveland nightclub at some point and later recovered. He kept it anyway. For someone who now parks a Rolls-Royce Ghost and two Aston Martins in the same building, holding onto that truck is as telling as anything else in this story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Football season is right around the corner, but fans won't have to wait until the start of the regular season to see some of the sport's biggest names on their televisions.

That is because State Farm released a new group of commercials starring Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo, Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, and Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti.

The idea behind the campaign is insurance is personal, as each of the spots featuring Mahomes highlights.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

One sees the Chiefs star speaking to Mike as "your favorite quarterback at your favorite restaurant with your favorite grandma," while the other has Mahomes and his head coach rejoining with a family for Ashley since she enjoys "sweet, sentimental stuff."

Skattebo's spot is based on finding a personal plan for the Giants running back himself, as Jake from State Farm learns all about his quirky approach to things:

As for Cignetti, the Indiana head coach starring in such a campaign with some of the biggest names in the NFL underscores his rise to stardom. All he did was lead Indiana, which was never known for its football success, to a national championship in just his second season at the helm.

And now he's in a national commercial campaign as a result.
