The Kansas City Current, the NWSL club closely tied to Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, reached a valuation of $275 million, highlighting the rapid growth of womenâs soccer. For Brittany, the moment carried extra meaning because her connection to the Current began years before Patrick officially joined the ownership group.Kansas City Current reaches $275 million valuationIn June 2025, Forbes ranked the Kansas City Current as the second-most valuable club in the National Womenâs Soccer League. The team was valued at $275 million, only slightly behind Angel City FC at $280 million.The Current also led the league in annual revenue, generating roughly $36 million. That figure placed the Kansas City club $1 million ahead of Angel City and offered another sign of how quickly the womenâs soccer market was expanding.The numbers were particularly striking because the Current had only begun playing regular-season matches in 2021. In just a few years, the club had grown from a new NWSL team into one of the leagueâs most valuable franchises.Brittany Mahomes celebrated the milestone on social media by sharing graphics highlighting the Currentâs valuation and league-leading revenue. Her reaction made sense given her personal history with the club.Brittany was one of the founders of the Kansas City womenâs soccer organization in 2020. A former collegiate soccer player at the University of Texas at Tyler, she had a connection to the sport long before the Current became a major business story.Patrick Mahomes later joined the ownership group, adding another high-profile sports figure to the clubâs growing profile.Patrick and Brittany Mahomesâ investment in womenâs soccerPatrick Mahomes has built an expanding sports portfolio beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs. His investments have included stakes connected to the Kansas City Royals, Sporting Kansas City and the Alpine Formula 1 team.Still, the Current stands out because of Brittanyâs early involvement. What began as her investment in womenâs soccer eventually became a family connection to a franchise that continued to gain financial momentum.When Patrick announced his ownership stake, he made his excitement clear, writing:âI am thankful for the chance to join @brittanylynne as part of the @thekccurrent ownership team,â Mahomes tweeted when he first purchased ownership stake. âShe and the Longs have done an incredible job building a world-class organization and I am excited to join another championship-caliber club as it continues to make history.âThe Mahomes family has also supported the Current away from the business side, often attending matches with their children. Their presence has helped bring additional attention to a club benefiting from the broader rise of womenâs sports.The $275 million valuation reported last year was therefore more than a financial milestone. It reflected the growing commercial strength of the NWSL and the vision behind the Currentâs rise. articles.title: Travis Kelce makes a major business move with 5% ownership in a product he has relied on for years while expanding his business empire
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce made another major move beyond the football field in January 2026, turning a product he has trusted for years into a business opportunity.
articles.body: Travis Kelce made another major move beyond the football field in January 2026, turning a product he has trusted for years into a business opportunity. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end announced a partnership with Sleep Number Corporation that gave him a 5% ownership stake in the mattress company. For Kelce, the deal is more than another celebrity endorsement. It connects his personal approach to recovery with his growing investment portfolio.Travis Kelceâs Sleep Number investment reflects his focus on recoveryKelceâs decision stands out because Sleep Number is already part of his daily routine. The NFL star said he has used the companyâs bed for years, making the investment a natural extension of an existing relationship rather than a simple promotional deal.His experience as a professional athlete also gives the partnership a clear purpose. Recovery is a major part of an NFL playerâs career, and quality sleep can become increasingly important as the physical demands of football build over time. Sleep Numberâs adjustable beds allow users to change their settings based on their comfort and recovery needs, something Kelce said has mattered throughout his career.Kelce explained his decision in a statement:âa constant through different seasons of my career and life. articles.title: NFL Execs Sound Off on Best International Cities to Host Franchise After Roger Goodell's Comments
articles.summary: London, Mexico City, Toronto and Berlin were mentioned as potential international cities to host NFL teams in light of commissioner Roger Goodell's recent statement that the league will have franchises outside the United States someday.
articles.body:
London, Mexico City, Toronto and Berlin were mentioned as potential international cities to host NFL teams in light of commissioner Roger Goodell's recent statement that the league will have franchises outside the United States someday.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler spoke with NFL team executives and asked them to select cities that would be the best places for the league to have a team if this does come to fruition.

London, per Fowler, was the "overwhelming favorite among league executives."

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

"It's got the facilities, a large economy and the population," an AFC executive told Fowler. "The fanbase there is passionate."

Per Fowler, London hosted 41 NFL games dating back to 1983. London will host three games in October this year, including two featuring the Jacksonville Jaguars on Oct. 11 and 18.

Mexico City and Toronto would certainly assuage any travel concerns about having an international team. Mexico City has hosted five regular season games and will add a sixth on Nov. 22 when the Minnesota Vikings play the San Francisco 49ers. Toronto, of course, is already host to numerous North American professional sports squads.

Berlin just hosted its first NFL game in 2025, when the Indianapolis Colts beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-25 in an overtime thriller. Early returns on that game were good, per an AFC executive to Fowler.

"Great atmosphere," the exec stated. "The (Colts-Falcons) game sold out really quickly, it was loud all game and there was definitely buzz in the city and downtown."

Berlin will also host games in 2027 and 2029, per Fowler.

Goodell made his belief clear that NFL teams will be outside the United States someday during an Aug. 18 interview with Markus Kuhn of RTL/ntv in Germany (h/t Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk).

"At some point, there will be NFL teams outside the USA," Goodell said. "I have no doubt that this will happen one day."

If so, there are some clear candidates, with London leading the way. In the meantime, the NFL continues its international series with nine regular season games outside the United States. The first-ever regular season game in Australia leads the way, with the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams playing on Thursday, Sept. 10 (Sept. 11 local time) in Melbourne.

articles.title: New 2027 NFL Mock Draft Drops by ESPN Expert, Arch Manning, Dante Moore, More Landing Spots Revealed
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of the 2026 college football and NFL regular seasons, ESPN NFL draft expert Jordan Reid released an early 2027 NFL mock draft on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Ahead of the start of the 2026 college football and NFL regular seasons, ESPN NFL draft expert Jordan Reid released an early 2027 NFL mock draft on Wednesday.

Reid projected quarterbacks to come off the board with each of the first three selections, and his top 10 picks look like this:

1. Cleveland Browns: Dante Moore, QB, Oregon

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

2. Arizona Cardinals: Arch Manning, QB, Texas

3. New York Jets: CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame

4. Miami Dolphins: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

5. Las Vegas Raiders: Cam Coleman, WR, Texas

6. Tennessee Titans: Dylan Stewart, EDGE, South Carolina

7. Carolina Panthers: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

8. New Orleans Saints: Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas

9. New York Giants: Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

10. Washington Commanders: Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

Reid included a hypothetical trade in his mock with the Miami Dolphins trading down from No. 1 to No. 4, allowing the Browns to move up and get their much-needed franchise quarterback.

The 2027 draft is shaping up to be a great one in terms of QB talent, and Reid believes Cleveland will go with Oregon's Dante Moore if it gets the opportunity.

Moore surprised many by returning to college rather than entering the 2026 NFL draft, but he now has a chance to firmly establish himself as the top pick in 2027.

In his first full season as a starter, Moore completed 71.8 percent of his passes for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions, and he figures to get even better in Oregon's high-powered offense.

The Browns' quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders was a mess leading up to head coach Todd Monken naming Watson the starter for 2026, but there is little doubt that the organization would love to avoid a similar situation next year, and selecting Moore would accomplish that goal.

Arizona has a similarly dire quarterback situation led by Jacoby Brissett, so it comes as little surprise that Reid has the Cardinals taking Texas quarterback Arch Manning at No. 2 overall.

While the nephew of legendary NFL quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning didn't dominate college football in his first season as a starter in 2025 like many expected, he acquitted himself well and has something to build upon in 2026.

Manning completed 61.4 percent of his passing attempts for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and seven picks, while also rushing for 399 yards and 10 scores last season.

With a year of starting experience under his belt and tons of offensive weaponry around him, everything is lining up for Manning to turn in a huge 2026 campaign ahead of the 2027 draft.

Rounding out the top three picks and the "Big Three" quarterbacks in Reid's mock is Notre Dame's CJ Carr.

As a redshirt freshman in 2025, Carr was highly impressive, completing 66.6 percent of his passes for 2,741 yards, 24 touchdowns and six interceptions.

It has been far too long since the Jets had a true franchise quarterback, and while they have a solid stopgap in Geno Smith for 2026, Carr could finally be the leader and face of the franchise that they have been searching for over the past several years.

As for the Dolphins, trading down from No. 1 to No. 4 in Reid's mock still lands them arguably the best overall player in the draft in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.

If the Dolphins trade down, it likely means that quarterback Malik Willis had a solid 2026 season, and getting him a weapon like Smith would only serve to elevate his play even more.

Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix made his preseason debut against the Green Bay Packers last week, marking his first live game action since he broke his ankle in the divisional round of the NFL playoffs in January.

Nix went 6-of-9 passing for 76 yards with one touchdown, leading two scoring drives before watching the rest of the game from the sideline. Denver coach Sean Payton was asked about Nix's return to action after Monday's practice.

"Good. I thought he did a good job," Payton said . "Yes, his movement skills were good. A little fast through one progression, but overall, he did a good job operating the huddle. He's moving around well. [He] had a couple big throws and felt very, very comfortable."

The Green Bay matchup also marked offensive coordinator Davis Webb 's first game calling plays for Nix.

"[It was] smooth, it was good," Payton said of Webb's play-calling. "Communication process was good. Yes, no issues. It was all clean."

The Los Angeles Rams are ready to go whether they have Aaron Donald back on their roster or not. If there was any doubt, Sean McVay has confirmed and made it clear they have plans for if AD is present, and they also have plans for if he's not. No surprise, really, but it's news nonetheless.

The media has been covering the Aaron Donald story throughout the offseason and to be fair, Turf Show Times has done its fair share of work too. Will Donald revise his contract? Does Aaron Donald really want to come back? Would Donald want to the risk the challenge of another NFL season?

So many questions for the Los Angeles Rams and Donald, and Week One against the San Francisco 49ers is fast approaching. There are a lot of takes on whether Donald will be back with the Rams early, later, much later or never. It doesn't seem like anyone with these takes actually knows.

Until anything is confirmed, everyone is waiting for Donald to confirm his plans. If Donald gets to do that on his time and not anyone else's, then know one "knows" what Donald is going to do except Donald. That doesn't stop anyone from speculating, and it can't stop the Rams from preparing.

"We've had plans if he's there, and if he's not," McVay said Tuesday, via the Los Angeles Times.

"Our thought process has been, 'let's look at a 53 with him and a 53 not including him and what does that look like. Whenever a decision is made, if that is the direction he goes where he wants to play, then we have plans accordingly and if not we have plans for those as well."

Contingency plans are common at this time of the season, especially as general managers are confronted with difficult decisions that must be made within the constraints of a 53-man roster. Los Angeles' is unique in that it will have one for the potential return of a franchise legend, but otherwise, it's business as usual."

"Discussing the situation on a recent episode, Mike Florio and his PFT co-host Chris Simms floated a scenario that splits the difference between Donald suiting up Week 1 and staying retired for good: re-signing him and immediately placing him on the physically unable to perform list.

Under that path, Donald would be permitted to work out on his own but couldn't practice with the Rams until the team opens a three-week practice window — at which point he'd get a ramp-up period before any decision on activating him to the 53-man roster."

"If he decides he wants to be able to do it, then the next conversations are: What is your ramp-up ?" McVay said Tuesday, via Benjamin Royer of the ocregister.com. "What does it look like to approach whenever that would be the first time that we think we make the most sense for him to impact and make a positive change with us?

"We've had to have a lot of fluidity and flexibility, and that's what I've had to learn over 10 years. But I think what's good is the thing that has served us well – and it's really the truth – is let's just stay one day at a time."

"Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett have been sidelined from practice for the last two weeks, but they're not the only starters out for the Los Angeles Rams on Tuesday. The Athletic's Nate Atkins noted at the start of practice that Alaric Jackson is absent, and Terrance Ferguson is working off to the side with the training staff like Nacua has been.

It's unclear why Jackson and Ferguson are not practicing; Nacua has a psoas injury, while Garrett is dealing with knee swelling."

That assessment arrives at an ideal time for a Rams team preparing to open the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football Instant Mock Draft, No. 7 Pick: Analysis, key takeaways and full roster
articles.summary: We're onto the No. 7 pick in our Yahoo Instant Mock Draft series for 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
As we get ready for the 2026 fantasy football season, there's no better way to prepare than doing mock drafts. And while live mock drafts will give us a great idea of how things might shake out, sometimes they're hit or miss and can be time consuming. Fortunately, Yahoo is offering its Instant Mock Draft tool again this season, available with your Fantasy Plus subscription. If you want to give the tool a spin for free, you can do an Instant Mock Draft for the first three rounds. Head here for more details .

If you're new to the instant mock tool, here are some of the benefits:

Draft immediately : That means no lobbies and no dropouts.

Drafts tailored to your league: No more guessing if a mock draft from a generic 12-team league with standard scoring matches your custom setup. Draft against our algorithm, which mimics your league opponents.

Test strategy: Simulate and try out different draft strategies from your exact draft slot. Find out which approach builds the strongest roster, then nail your live draft with real-time, on-the-clock recommendations.

In this series, I'll be performing an instant mock draft out of each pick slot for 12-team leagues with default half-PPR scoring. Today, we're picking a team from the No. 7 spot. Below is the full roster, plus key takeaways.

No. 1 | No. 2 | No. 3 | No. 4 | No. 5 | No. 6 | No. 7 | No. 8 | No. 9 | No. 10 | No. 11 | No. 12

QB: Caleb Williams, CHI RB: Rhamondre Stevenson, NE RB: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, WAS WR: Amon-Ra St. Brown, DET WR: Nico Collins, HOU TE: George Kittle, SF FLEX: Tee Higgins, CIN Kicker: Tyler Bass, BUF Defense: Patriots Bench: Ladd McConkey, LAC Bench: R.J. Harvey, DEN Bench: Mike Washington Jr., LV Bench: De'Zhaun Stribling, SF Bench: Oronde Gadsden II, LAC Bench: Woody Marks, HOU

I did a mix of thinking like Yahoo analyst Scott Pianowski and a pure Zero RB build. I did a Zero RB look a few mocks ago but it wasn't as drastic as this one; I didn't take my first back until Round 7 with Stevenson here. Normally, I'd be willing to go with three WRs (the max you can start) and then pivot over to RB, but this approach allows you to get solid options at QB and TE so you aren't concerned about streaming much. Let's break down the team a bit.

I was faced with this decision in the first round and opted for the Sun God over the reigning WR champ from a season ago. I think there's plenty that would point to regression for Jaxon Smith-Njigba — Klint Kubiak's departure, Kenneth Walker III leaving, defenses around the NFL adjusting, etc.

One thing Pianowski highlighted are some offenses that have a tight usage tree and make for quality teams to target in fantasy. So we pressed the easy button and went with St. Brown, who has been arguably the most consistent fantasy wideout over the past four seasons. In that stretch, he hasn't finished outside the top 10 at his position and was top-five three times, plus top-15 overall in fantasy in two of those campaigns. There's so much working in Detroit's favor, from the coaching staff to Jared Goff at QB to playing most games indoors. Having the chance to take a player like St. Brown in this range is why Joel Smyth has the No. 7 slot ranked fourth if you can choose your own first-round pick in 2026.

Collins, Higgins and McConkey round out the WR room. The Texans lost Jayden Higgins, and while Collins was always going to be a target hog, that sentiment got a boost. Higgins is on another one of those destination teams for Pianowski in the Bengals with very little usage competition outside him, Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown. McConkey is a Year 3 breakout candidate and should bounce back with the Chargers' O-line in better health.

There were a few QBs on the board alongside Williams — Dak Prescott and Justin Herbert to name a few. It felt like a reach on Dak, whom I think has a capped ceiling and some age concerns. Herbert would have made an OK stack with McConkey but I also have him as my WR4, so I wouldn't want to force myself into pairing Herbert and McConkey week-to-week. Williams was quietly the QB5 in overall fantasy scoring in 2025 and while I hate to admit it as a Packers fan, he should only improve with another year under Ben Johnson. Plus, all those weapons — Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland, Luther Burden III, D'Andre Swift. I also think Williams has some untapped, sneaky Aaron Rodgers-esque rushing upside this season.

Kittle got an encouraging report on his recovery from an Achilles tear and appears on track to not start the season on the PUP list. Now, this doesn't mean he will play Week 1. The 49ers could hold him out for a bit. But I feel fine rolling out secondary options or a TE streaming (Jake Tonges) early in the season until Kittle gets up to speed. Kittle's ADP is rising and I did reach on him a bit, but even in this range he has a great chance of returning value as someone who was the TE3 in FPPG last season. San Fran would be one injury to Mike Evans away from Kittle being the clear top receiving option on the offense. He'd be a red-zone target hog and give me a great floor/ceiling combo with this build.

There are plenty of solid late-round RB options that come a bit after the RB Dead Zone . I also wanted to grab a few RBs who have receiving chops, elevating their floor for PPR formats. JCM as my RB2 gives me some worry, though his ADP has been on the rise lately . He's also a favorite sleeper of Justin Boone's for a reason . We now know TreVeyon Henderson is at least a little banged up, though he should be fine. Still, Stevenson was already ahead of him on the depth chart, it's a top offense in New England and he can catch passes.

Harvey and Marks feel like two second-year backs who are being grossly overlooked. Are we really expecting an oft-injured J.K. Dobbins or a rookie to be ahead of Harvey in Denver? Sure, there are between-the-tackles concerns but we know for sure Harvey will be involved in what should be a solid passing attack. Same for Marks. David Montgomery has a lot of miles and should see plenty of goal-line work. But the coaching staff may want to keep Monty fresh and Marks should be in there in passing situations at least. As players available well outside the top 100 picks, you could do worse than Harvey and Marks as your backup RBs in fantasy.

Oh yeah, and we almost forgot about rising star Mike Washington Jr. In a Zero RB build, I want to target players with a path to RB1 status. Even if Ashton Jeanty misses a week or two, great, Washington is probably an RB1 in those weeks. If this injury lingers at all, Washington likely has RB2/3 upside, plus we know he'll be involved even when Jeanty is healthy, given Kubiak's play-calling.

Zero RB isn't for the faint of heart. You need to be very prepared with RB targets late in the draft and feel confident in those picks, otherwise you're going to leave the draft feeling a bit panicked. Also, keep in mind that you have WR depth for a reason. We know we only have three spots for WRs and if all four are performing at a high level (and someone on the bench emerges), we can trade that depth for RB help. I'd classify this strategy as a bit more advanced, so be sure to read up on all our free content here in the Draft Kit .

articles.title: Before you go RB-RB to start your fantasy draft, consider this warning
articles.summary: Something happened last season that hasn't happen since 2011 or earlier. It's a statistical outlier disguised as a new norm.
articles.body:
Something happened last season that hasn't happened since 2011 or earlier. It's a statistical outlier disguised as a new norm. If you're planning to take two running backs in the first two rounds of your fantasy draft, consider the following.

The top-10 RBs -- based on ADP -- entering Week 1 last year collectively missed only four games all season, accounting for only 2% of their teams' contests. How unusual was that? Across the previous 14 seasons, dating back to 2012, the top-10 ADP running backs had missed an average of 19% of their games.

What happened in 2011 or earlier? No clue, because reliable ADPs are hard to find prior to 2012. So, for all intents and purposes, last year's top-10 RBs were durable to an unprecedented degree.

As a result, most of them crushed it fantasy-wise; that's what happens when great starters stay on the field week after week. Also, as a result, most of them are once again in the top 10 in ADP.

Not surprising, and also quite concerning, especially considering Christian McCaffrey's massive injury/regression risks , Saquon Barkley's advancing age and high-end handcuff status, and Jonathan Taylor's extensive injury history, which most managers seem to have forgotten after last year's MVP-level output.

To be clear, some RBs are safer than others. But collectively, what happened last year was an anomaly. We should expect this year's top 10 to miss at least 15% of their games. Hopefully you pick the right guys.

For a deeper dive into the overall risks of going RB-RB in your draft, listen to this recent podcast episode .

A deal with the NFL, critics say, puts the credibility of that entire probe in serious doubt.Why is The Athletic being called hypocritical over the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel investigation?The criticism isn't coming from anonymous corners of the internet. OutKick columnist Armando Salguero wrote directly about the contradiction at the heart of The Athletic's situation, and his words cut straight to the point."The Athletic is presumably in the throes of this conflict of interest investigation of a former reporter with an NFL coach while at the same time engaging in talks to enter into a conflict of interest situation with the NFL. Got it," Salguero wrote.He didn't stop there. "That raises a sizeable inconsistency. The Athletic is presumably investigating Russini for possibly engaging in a questionable relationship with an NFL coach at a time it is weighing whether to get in bed with the NFL."The argument isn't complicated. The Athletic has strict editorial guidelines that govern its staff, and those guidelines were central to why the Russini probe was launched in the first place. An institutional partnership with the NFL would place the outlet in essentially the same position it is investigating Russini for. Salguero made that parallel explicit: "So will The Athletic, on the one hand trying to avoid the appearance of a conflict of interest, allow an affiliation with the NFL that violates its own guidelines by calling into question its credibility?"That's not a rhetorical flourish. It's a real question with real consequences for how seriously anyone should take the outcome of this investigation.What happens to the Dianna Russini investigation if The Athletic partners with the NFL?That's where things get genuinely murky. Others have already questioned whether The Athletic will even release the findings of the Russini investigation if the NFL partnership is finalized. The incentive to publish a critical report about a league you're now financially aligned with is, to put it plainly, not great.The scandal itself began when Russini and Vrabel were photographed together at a resort in Arizona, appearing to hug, hold hands, and lounge by the pool. It turned into a months-long tabloid story, with fans combing through old interviews, social media posts, and even Spotify playlists for more context. Russini resigned from The Athletic, and Vrabel stepped away from his Patriots duties on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft to attend counseling with his family.Since then, both have largely gone quiet. Vrabel has appeared at press conferences. Russini has not addressed the situation publicly beyond her initial statement and resignation letter. She deleted her social media accounts and recently referred to herself as a "former journalist" in text messages that leaked to a New York Times reporter, suggesting she isn't planning a return to sports media.The investigation, meanwhile, sits in an uncomfortable place. An outlet probing editorial bias while negotiating closer ties to the very organization at the center of that bias story isn't exactly a clean look. Whether The Athletic acknowledges that tension publicly or quietly lets the partnership reshape what the probe produces, the outcome either way is going to draw scrutiny.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lose your fantasy league, suffer the consequences: Inside the wild world of last-place punishments
articles.summary: As last-place punishments get more elaborate, humiliating and downright diabolical, the race to avoid the bottom has become almost as intense as the race to...
articles.body:
On the eve of a prestigious amateur bodybuilding competition last month in Boca Raton, Florida, one participant called organizer Maria Bellando with a pressing question.

"Is it mandatory to shave your whole body?" Ty Harrelson asked.

No, it isn't mandatory, Bellando replied, but every bodybuilder does it.

"Make sure you at least shave your privates because we can't have hair in that area," Bellando added.

When Harrelson showed up for registration the next morning, Bellando picked him out before he even revealed his name. Harrelson's legs and arms were unshaven and his spray tan was at least a half dozen shades lighter than anyone else's. The 26-year-old asked to buy posing trunks on the premises because he didn't own any.

Harrelson appeared even more out of his element to Bellando when he stepped on stage in front of an audience of several hundred to compete in the men's heavyweight division. It wasn't just that his broad-shouldered everyman physique lacked the extreme muscle definition of the Herculean competitors beside him. The dead giveaway was Harrelson glancing over at the poses they were doing and then trying his best to mimic them.

"Ninety-nine percent of people that are competing in our shows are serious athletes that have been prepping and training and doing this stuff for years," Bellando said. "We knew there was something strange going on, but we didn't know what it was."

It wasn't until after the show that Bellando learned Harrelson did not participate in the NPC Southern States Championships by choice. Entering a bodybuilding competition was Harrelson's punishment for finishing last in his fantasy football league last season.

Last-place punishments have long been a fantasy football staple, providing incentive for a league's bottom-dwelling managers to keep trying after they've already been eliminated from playoff contention. In recent years, leagues have become increasingly creative and ruthless with their punishments, making the battle to avoid last place as high stakes and pressure-packed as the race to finish first.

One recent fantasy loser suffered the indignity of taking a blowup doll on a dinner date . Another had to run a roadside lemonade stand in the dead of winter. A third dressed up like the "Very Hungry Caterpillar" and consumed the exact sequence of food items from Eric Carle's famous 1969 children's book.

The last-place finisher in Caitlin Clark 's league completed a 17-hour bus ride with no screens and no entertainment, the Indiana Fever star told the New Heights Podcast last December. That's nothing compared to how far podcaster Joel Solomon traveled for his punishment. The last-place finisher in Solomon's league had to watch Super Bowl LX in exile this past February from an international city of the league champion's choosing.

"Has anyone else ever flown to Mumbai, India, to watch the Super Bowl in a hotel lobby at 5:30 in the morning as a fantasy league punishment?" Solomon posted to X, alongside two photos showing him watching the Seahawks demolish the Patriots on his laptop.

Diabolical punishments typically don't require the last-place finisher to fork over thousands of dollars on airfare and hotels. A group of friends from Buffalo, New York, recently dreamed up a clever idea for those in a more modest tax bracket.

"JOSH SUCKS AT FANTASY," read the billboard Luke Baxter and his leaguemates rented in February 2025 at the corner of Kenmore and Elmwood Avenues in North Buffalo. A photo of Josh also adorned the billboard, as did a plea from Josh's leaguemates to "roast him" at a Google Voice number they provided.

It was Baxter's responsibility to propose punishment ideas before the 2024 fantasy season after he finished last the previous year and endured a polar plunge in an icy lake as penance. His mind immediately went to punishments that wouldn't be over so quickly.

"Thirty seconds of pain wasn't enough," Baxter quipped. "I wanted the next last-place finisher's pain to last a whole month."

The billboard Baxter chose was a five-minute drive from where he and his leaguemates once went to high school together. More than once, Baxter touched base with Josh to make sure the punishment wasn't too extreme. Each time, his friend reassured him that it would be a fun story to tell their kids one day.

Over the 30 days that the billboard stayed up, hundreds of texts and voice messages poured in, some from former classmates, teachers and coworkers and others from complete strangers.

"My favorite voicemail was from an Uber driver," Baxter said. "The whole car started roasting Josh — the driver and his passengers."

Suggesting a painfully awkward last-place punishment backfired on professional hockey player Connor Marritt. When he finished last in his league last season, the Tahoe Knight Monsters forward had to endure the indignity of doing it himself.

Borrowing from a funny video he stumbled across while scrolling on TikTok, Marritt proposed that the last-place finisher in his league would have to play nine holes of golf with strangers without using a golf ball. Worse yet, the last-place finisher would be forbidden from revealing that a fantasy football punishment was the reason he was play-acting every shot.

Everyone in Marritt's league became friends while attending the same youth hockey academy in British Columbia. They immediately embraced Marritt's punishment proposal. And, of course, they took pleasure in it even more when an ill-fated early-season Deebo Samuel-for-George Pickens trade put Marritt in jeopardy of the dreaded last-place finish.

"It came down to the final Monday night of the season," Marritt recalled. "When the second-to-last-place team pulled out a victory, I was like, 'Oh my God, I'm going to have to do this."

To his credit, Marritt leaned in. All the way in.

Randomly paired with two older men named Graham and David at the Michaelbrook Golf Club in British Columbia, Marritt smoothly pretended that he "had a really bad case of the shanks" and that hitting imaginary shots was a "visualization technique" to fix his swing. Throughout the TikTok video of his round discreetly filmed last month by one of his leaguemates, Marritt can be seen admiring a supposedly perfect tee shot, checking his yardage and bemoaning an occasional mishit.

At one point, he points to an empty spot a couple feet from the hole and asks Graham to tap in his imaginary putt. Later, when David asks earnestly if he can walk through Marritt's putting line, Marritt somehow avoids breaking character and urges him not to worry about golf etiquette.

"I couldn't believe how supportive Graham and David were," Marritt said. "Like, if it was me on the other end, I'd be like, 'Who is this whack job going around with no ball? Golf has gotten this guy so messed up that he thinks this is going to help.' But they were offering me swing tips."

Video of Marritt's punishment did millions of views after Yahoo and ESPN reposted it, but his two graying co-stars were unaware of it until the hockey player reached out and told them they were "getting some very positive reviews."

"They were great sports about it," Marritt said. "They want to play another nine holes."

The venue for Cole Bray's January 2025 last-place punishment was Wake Forest's largest on-campus dining hall. Bray's leaguemates decided to publicly shame the finance major by requiring him to walk a marathon while weaving between buffet stations and crowded seating areas.

For 9.5 tedious hours, Bray walked the same tedious figure-eight-shaped route , breaking the monotony by listening to music, switching directions or grabbing an occasional glass of water from a friend. The more laps around the dining hall Bray completed, the more confused stares he received.

"I honestly wish I had something that said I suck at fantasy, so that people knew what I was doing," Bray said. "I remember this group of girls looking at me like, 'Has this kid lost his mind?' There was an employee in the dining hall who thought I was having a mental breakdown."

More people caught on to what Bray was doing by the time he neared the 26.2-mile mark. The room erupted in cheers when Bray jogged through a toilet paper finish line. A dining hall employee even presented him with a tiny plastic trophy in honor of his accomplishment.

"I had some blisters on my feet, but it wasn't too hard," Bray said. "Honestly, the worst part was having to walk back to the dorm afterward."

To Harrelson, the physical pain of completing a marathon sounds manageable compared to the crippling anxiety that he endured. He shed about 30 pounds training for his bodybuilding debut, yet the idea of posing on stage in a red Speedo still terrified him.

"I have never been more scared of doing something in my life," Harrelson said. "I was sweating and shaking, and then I mentally blacked out. I don't even really remember being on stage."

His buddies, of course, remember. A half dozen of them were in the crowd laughing hysterically. The video that one of them captured of Harrelson in the bodybuilding show has nearly 650,000 likes on TikTok and even recently aired on ABC's Good Morning America.

The TikTok video was how Bellando learned the real reason that Harrelson participated in her bodybuilding competition. When the video began to circulate across social media and beyond, friends started texting Bellando, 'You're famous now!"

When Bellando and Harrelson subsequently spoke on the phone, she asked him why he didn't tell her he was fulfilling a fantasy football punishment.

"I thought I was going to get in trouble," Harrelson said.

Bellando assured him that she thought it was a fun idea and that she was grateful for the free publicity.

Among those who got a kick out of Harrelson moonlighting as a bodybuilder was his boss at Native Construction Group. Now in Harrelson's office there's a life-sized cutout of him flexing in his red posing trunks.

"I've had distant family text me and my mom like, 'Oh, is this Ty?'" Harrelson said. "People we don't even really talk to, people that live in other states. I can't go anywhere down here without people asking about it. It was pretty crazy."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Draft Strategy 2026, Latest Mock Draft and Cheat Sheet Tips
articles.summary: If you pooled the thoughts of 100 fantasy football experts together, you might wind up getting pulled 100 different directions.
articles.body:
If you pooled the thoughts of 100 fantasy football experts together, you might wind up getting pulled 100 different directions.

Just like NFL teams have different ways to big, that same optionality exists in the fantasy realm.

You, obviously, hold control of the roster you're putting together. If you want to open a draft with three consecutive running backs or four wideouts in a row, you can. Or maybe you see all of those advising folks to wait on tight ends and quarterbacks as a simple way for you to snag top talents at both spots.

We can't tell you which strategy is right or wrong for you, but we can help you form that opinion with a look at a mock draft, cheat sheet-style positional rankings and our favorite team-building tips.

Know your league rules and draft according to them.

Fantasy leagues come in all sizes and play styles, so you need to make note of any particulars to your own. At the very least, get your bases covered. A smaller league, for instance, should embolden you to take more risks, since the waiver wire should always be well-stocked. A league that awards six points for a passing touchdown rather than the typical four elevates all quarterbacks, but especially pocket passers with loud volume.

You need to know exactly what your league entails before you enter its draft room. Because while general advice is generally helpful, it's really just a guide that you have to tweak to ensure it applies to exactly what you need.

Knowing a player's average draft position is helpful in the sense that you have a rough idea of where they are normally picked. But you shouldn't treat these numbers as absolute truths. You don't want to miss out on players you like or add players you don't just because the ADP data says you should.

Different host sites have their own rankings, too, making you more exposed to the whims of that site's experts. Remember, this is your roster, not theirs, so you'd be better off having your own rankings to consult.

Have a strategy, but be willing to adapt.

Entering a draft, you might have a pretty clear idea of what you're aiming to do at the top. If you see value in stockpiling early running backs or waiting longer than most at quarterback for your favorite sleeper, those are absolutely practices you should aim to put in play.

Just remember that things inevitably won't go all according to plan. Other managers have their own ideas, and they'll overlap with yours often enough to deny you that dream build you initially envisioned. And that's OK. Stay patient, adjust to what's happening in front of you, and you'll be fine.

articles.title: The top 16 most likely candidates to be fantasy football's overall WR1 in 2026
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Harmon breaks down 16 of the game's best wide receivers to see who could claim the throne in 2026.
articles.body:
Over the past several seasons, I've discussed the "three pillars" a player must have in his outlook to become the fantasy WR1 overall. Our last three WR1 overall finishers have been CeeDee Lamb (2023), Ja'Marr Chase (2024) and Puka Nacua (2025); that should put a finer point on how much the variables paint the correct picture.

Must own a dominant target share in his offense.

Must be tethered to an efficient quarterback/offense.

Must be verifiably great, not just good, at football.

Using those pillars, let's take a look at my top 16 ranked receivers — which make up my first two tiers at the position, including a beefy Tier 2 to exemplify the strength of this position — to examine how clean their paths are to push for the WR1 overall title in 2026. You can get access to those tiered rankings and much more in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook . For now, let's get into the list.

Over the last three seasons combined, Ja'Marr Chase owns a 27.6% share of his team's targets, second-highest at the wide receiver position. As Chase's career has gone on, we've seen the Bengals increase their efforts to move the elite wideout around the formation to get easy-button looks. He will be an annual contender to lead the NFL in targets.

Whenever Joe Burrow is on the field, this answer is an easy yes. Burrow has missed a good chunk of time over the last few seasons, but even when the quarterback isn't on the field from 2023 to 2025, Chase is still targeted on almost 27% of his routes and averages 2.12 yards per route, which would have ranked 14th last season.

Another obvious yes. You can argue that Chase is the best receiver in the NFL right now — it's a two-horse race between him and Justin Jefferson , in my opinion. Chase is not only an elite ball-winner and playmaker after the catch, but he's really undercredited as a craftsman-level route runner.

Since Puka Nacua entered the NFL in 2023, no receiver has been used at a higher rate when he's on the football field. Nacua leads all wide receivers in targets per route run with a 33% rate the last three seasons. He gets layup designer looks and high-yield downfield targets.

Matthew Stafford won the NFL MVP last season, in case you missed it. The health of the 38-year-old quarterback will always be something to monitor. However, even if he misses time, I trust Sean McVay's overall offensive ecosystem and Nacua's heavy layup role to insulate the offense from quarterback chaos.

You can dispel any notion that Nacua is some creation of McVay's scheme or simply a product of Stafford. Those variables obviously matter but Nacua has developed into a star in his own right as a strong separator and someone who can win at the catch point and after the catch.

Amon-Ra St. Brown became a full-time player for the Lions in the back half of his rookie season in 2021 and walked into the following season as their top receiver. Since that 2022 campaign, he leads the NFL with a 28.2% share of the Lions offense. That's 623 targets over 66 total games. My colleague Scott Pianowski likes to say certain players should walk off the bus with 10 targets banked for the game ahead. Few players are closer to that being a reality than St. Brown the last four seasons.

Even in a somewhat down season for the Lions, the offense still ranked fifth in explosive play rate, seventh in points per drive and eighth in dropback EPA. Drew Petzing, as the guy to execute Dan Campbell's vision rather than John Morton, will prove to be an upgrade, particularly given the down-to-down consistency in the run game.

I think we've run out of reasons to consider St. Brown as anything but an elite player at the position. Since 2022, he ranks seventh in yards per route, third in first downs per route and second in successful targets per route. My charting in Reception Perception confirms he has improved as a press-coverage-beater every season, finishing at the 94th percentile this past season.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 35.8% target share is the highest for a wide receiver in the last decade. The Seahawks could get more out of some ancillary options in the passing game but at present, don't have anyone to slice out more than 5% of his target share. He can lose that and still be a volume monster.

The Seahawks were ninth in explosive play rate and 15th in success rate last season — the run game was lacking more than the aerial attack from an efficiency standpoint. Overall, they were a top-12-15 NFL offense in 2025. While they are retaining most of their talent and I certainly don't regard Sam Darnold as a negative variable at this stage, they did lose Klint Kubiak this offseason. That matters, as new OC Brian Fleury is an unknown.

Smith-Njigba is a Tier 1 NFL receiver and was the best route runner I charted on film last season. He's an unbelievably talented player who blends both explosive-play potential and route-by-route consistency.

When CeeDee Lamb was on the field last season, he owned a 29.2% target share of the Cowboys offense. He out-targeted his high-profile teammate (22.4%) 117 to 90 in those 14 games. Between 2023 and 2024, Lamb was targeted on 29% of his routes, fourth-most among wide receivers in that span. No matter the conditions, Lamb is a target monster.

The Cowboys ranked fifth in points per drive and third in success rate. I think they can even take a step forward in 2026. Dak Prescott is a top-10 NFL quarterback and this is one of the best ecosystems going right now.

Lamb may have been a slightly diminished version of himself while playing through a high-ankle sprain for multiple games last year. He was still excellent. No questions about his skill set and ability as we move to 2026.

Even as Justin Jefferson finished outside the top-35 wide receivers in points per game last season, he still owned a 30.1% target share of the Vikings offense. There's no doubting that the Vikings do an excellent job making sure he gets his looks even when he faces some of the most difficult coverage assignments on a weekly basis.

Among 40 quarterbacks who took 200 snaps last season, J.J. McCarthy ranked 37th in EPA per play and 36th in success rate. Things will be better than that in 2026. Fellow Vikings starter Carson Wentz (207 snaps) ranked 19th in success rate and 25th in EPA per play. Jefferson averaged 6.8 catches and 95.4 yards in the five games Wentz started last season — 4.2 catches and 47.6 yards per game in all other contests.

Kyler Murray ranked 22nd in EPA per play in an offense that didn't fit his skill set from 2023 to 2025. He's not a perfect solution and the Vikings offense is a little more volatile under Kevin O'Connell than most like to admit. However, all this combined should be good enough for an average to slightly above-average attack, which is good enough for Jefferson, even if the answer to this question is no.

If anyone is putting any significant percentage of the blame for Jefferson's lack of production last at the foot of the future Hall of Fame wideout, they need a serious reality check.

When Nico Collins was on the field last season, he owned a hulking 29.6% share of the Texans' targets. From 2023 to 2024, he averaged the same targets per route rate (27.1%) as St. Brown. Injuries have been a question but when he's on the field, Collins is the engine of the Texans' passing game.

Efficient offense/QB: Yes, with some caveats.

I will go out on a limb here and answer mostly in the affirmative. Yes, the last thing we saw from C.J. Stroud was a catastrophe:

However, that unfairly shaped how people viewed Stroud's 2025 season, when he was a top-10 quarterback in EPA per play during the regular season. He was sandwiched between Darnold and Patrick Mahomes . Houston overall ranked 13th in dropback EPA and 12th in rate of drives to end in a score. If the running game — 31st in success rate since Stroud entered the league — can hold up its end of the bargain, I bet this can be the best offense we've seen from Houston in a few years.

Despite running out as a near-exclusive X-receiver for years, Collins has been one of the most efficient wide receivers in the game.

He did all this while playing with the quarterback most are afraid of, too. Collins is an elite man and press coverage-beater in Reception Perception , as well. He's a top 5-6 wideout in my real-life rankings.

Before Drake London got hurt in Week 11, he was averaging 10.4 targets per game, ranking second behind only Chase. He was the WR3 in per-game fantasy scoring. The 2025 season was going to be London's true eruption campaign, but it was interrupted by a PCL injury. He's been targeted on 28.8% of his routes the last two seasons, the fourth-highest rate in that span, and ranks eighth overall since he entered the league in 2022. No matter what goes on around him, London is a volume hog.

Of course, we've seen London push beyond the limits of his quarterback situation, even just last season, as shown above. He will be productive regardless. However, I still struggle to see the Falcons reaching even an average level of passing efficiency with their current situation behind center. There's also a small part of me that's worried London gets relegated back to X-receiver duties after he was perfectly deployed as the movement Z and big slot under Zac Robinson. It's just a theory, but it would complicate matters further under an offensive coaching staff I'm mixed on overall.

I'd posit that London is one of my favorite wide receivers in the NFL right now. He's so emblematic of where the game is going with a new archetype of WR1s who can win at X-receiver but are maximized all across the formation. He is an obvious top-10 player at the position.

As noted above, George Pickens had a 22.4% target share of the Cowboys offense when Lamb was on the field. That's perfectly fine but not quite dominant. His 22.6% targets per route rate ranked 27th at the position last season. We've already seen Pickens has the upside to be that volume hog when Lamb misses time, but if the WR1 is healthy, there's a capped ceiling for the latter.

Check the Lamb section above. This offense will cook in 2026.

Pickens is now, at worst, one of the premier WR2s in the NFL. You can make an argument that he proved he could be an effective No. 1 while holding down outlier boundary usage in 2025. He's become a much more well-rounded player than he was in his first two seasons with the Steelers . He's a joy to watch these days, particularly against man coverage.

Chris Olave handled a whopping 29.4% of the Saints targets in Weeks 1 to 17 before sitting out the final game of the season. That ranked sixth in that span, just behind Jefferson. His targets per route ranked eighth on the year. There was a chance that Round 1 rookie Jordyn Tyson could have eaten into that workload in 2026 to some degree but now the rookie is set to miss over a month of regular season action. After developing pristine chemistry with Tyler Shough in the back half of the season, expect Olave to be a volume hog again.

I'm high on what the Saints coaching staff showed last season. The team ranked first in seconds per play while operating at a fast pace and first in rate of dropbacks with pre-snap motion. The results weren't great overall, but they picked up when Tyler Shough took over. With another season in the system and behind a good offensive line, I think this can be a top-15 unit in the NFL. That is still a projection, so it would be disingenuous to write it in pen.

Anyone with eyeballs can tell Olave is a WR1 in the NFL. He's been in my inner circle of premier route runners for a few seasons now and was employed perfectly last season to express his skills. The only critique you can lob at his game is that he's a YAC monster. Otherwise, he checks all the boxes.

Since the 2022 season, DeVonta Smith has taken 698 snaps without A.J. Brown on the field. He's run 205 routes in that span was targeted on 28.8% of them, good for 2.36 yards per route. I feel comfortable projecting him for the lion's share of the volume in Philadelphia 's passing game this season. However, Round 1 receiver Makai Lemon could soak up layup looks in the back half of the year, and Dontayvion Wicks won't be a nothing-burger in the distribution. That should at least be acknowledged.

Last season, the Eagles ranked 13th in explosive play rate but 24th in success rate. They could still hit big plays but weren't effective down-to-down. I'm really excited about the idea of Sean Mannion pushing the scheme forward but there's no question that it will be an adjustment for Jalen Hurts after he's played quite a different style of football. That's not to say he can't do it but we have to admit it will be an adjustment.

Smith has been an overqualified WR2 alongside an elite-level WR1 in A.J. Brown for some time now. We even have plenty of evidence from early in his career that he can handle being the top guy on the team while playing as the X-receiver — he hit a team-high 916 yards in 2021. We noted the yards-per-route figure (2.36), which is a teammate-sensitive stat even if fantasy analysts hate to admit it, without Brown over the last four years. He's absolutely capable of being the top dog in a passing tree.

As long as Chase is active, Tee Higgins is unlikely to ever hit the target share ceiling needed to compete for this title. When Higgins and Chase have been on the field together the last two years, Higgins has a 17.2% target share to 29.9% for Chase. This is a clear WR1/WR2 hierarchy.

See the Chase section above. When Burrow has been on the field the last two seasons, Higgins averages 14.1 points per game and 2.01 yards per route run, which would vault him to WR7 and 19th in those stats. The ecosystem is right for this vertical X-receiver archetype.

Verifiably great at football: Pretty much yes

Higgins is a No. 2 wide receiver in the NFL to me, but is one of the premier second-fiddles. He can push right up to the line of being a WR1, and frankly, for many teams, he would be their best option. He would have amazing contingent value if Chase ever missed games.

When he was on the field for the Miami Dolphins last year and Tyreek Hill was not, Waddle was targeted on 26.7% of his routes and owned a 31% share of the Dolphins offense. I don't doubt Waddle's ability to command and dominate targets but in a Denver offense that has an established quality X-receiver in Courtland Sutton and some quality ancillary pass-catchers, that massive, north-of-26% target share may not be realistic. I just won't rule it out completely.

The Broncos offense ranked fourth in success rate but 21st in explosive play rate last season. That latter figure is precisely why Waddle is in the fold. I'm banking on Waddle having a diet version of a Stefon Diggs-like effect for Bo Nix , just as the former Bills wideout had on Josh Allen . Nix has been a solid quarterback so far, ranking 17th in EPA per play last year, but Waddle will push him to the next level.

By any stat, Waddle is clearly a great receiver, ranking eighth in first downs per route run among WRs with 200-plus routes last season, 12th in yards per route and 11th in successful targets per route. He's also an excellent full-field separator who gets open and makes plays with the ball in his hands. We'll also see him play a role much better suited to his skills than the heavy outside, on-ball diet he enjoyed in Miami.

Even if some of his rookie season was overinflated by Brian Daboll's scheme that spams a top target, as opposed to designing a strong offense, Nabers has been targeted at an extremely high rate through his NFL career. Nabers' 2024 targets per route rate of 30.9% ranks 13th highest for any receiver season since 2015. There are some interesting complementary players on the Giants roster but no one at the level to eat into Nabers' projection.

Jaxson Dart was a more than reasonable starting quarterback for the Giants as a rookie. He played almost all of the season without Nabers, so that will help this season. However, I still have enough questions about the overall environment around him, particularly the Matt Nagy and Greg Roman landscape to project this offense outside the top-20 units. Nabers will need to handle absurd volume to flirt with a WR1 overall finish, which isn't impossible but less likely since he's coming off a major injury.

When Nabers is fully operational, he's absolutely at the level of a wideout who can earn this title. The first designation carries a lot of weight; while Nabers looks on track to play in Week 1, we don't know for sure when he'll be at his best. However, when we last saw Nabers, he was playing at the level of a receiver who is knocking on the door to be a true Tier 1 WR in the NFL. That's not a phrase I use lightly.

Zay Flowers owned a 29% target share in the 2025 Ravens offense. That was fifth-most among wide receivers. He's in position to do it once again in 2026. Not only did Flowers just outright earn those looks, but most of the same cast of characters will also return in the pass-catching group this year; guys we already know he can significantly out-target. Rookie third-rounder Ja'Kobi Lane will be a factor after a strong offseason but he's more of a vertical contested-catch target, which doesn't lead to a ton of volume. Flowers needs more raw targets, which may come with a new offense but his share is secure.

Lamar Jackson didn't have his best season, as he played through injuries and struggled. However, it will take more than one down year for me to change my stance on him being a clear favorable force in this regard. I'm bullish on Declan Doyle's offense being a positive as well, as he looks to bring in much of what he was doing with Ben Johnson last year.

Since he entered the league in 2023, Flowers ranks 10th in yards and 14th in yards per route run. He's put together a strong résumé to be considered, at least, a top-20 receiver in the NFL and has gotten better every year. He's cut out the mistakes that haunted him at the catch point and with the ball in his hands earlier in his career. Flowers has been a premier zone-beater in all three of his NFL seasons, per Reception Perception, and took a major jump against press last year — that could help him cross the final frontier of being a higher touchdown scorer to truly access a high ceiling.

A.J. Brown certainly hopes he's the clear top target of this offense with some room to spare to No. 2. Brown had a 26.1% target share in the Eagles' passing game and he wasn't 100% for parts of last season. While the Patriots have some nice complementary players around him, it would be a major upset if Brown didn't clear 25% in 2026.

Drake Maye finished first in EPA per play, second in success rate and first in completion rate over expected, all while leading the NFL in air yards per target. He did it all with subpar protection and no stars in the skill-position group. Maye struggled in the playoffs and that's a part of his story. Yet, I'm comfortable calling him an obvious top-10 player at the position and an ascendent young player. He more than meets the requirement.

I have written about this extensively over the offseason , but I think we may have seen the first signs of decline in Brown's game last year. Yes, he was better in the back half, as I wrote in his Reception Perception Profile , after he got healthy from a hamstring injury, and the Patriots can push off some of this decline by moving him around the formation more often .

However, I just don't think it should be completely dismissed for a 29-year-old receiver with a history of knee issues that, reportedly, caused some teams to back out of the trade pursuit. Ultimately, I hope I'm wrong to be concerned.

articles.title: Dak Prescott emerges as NFL MVP dark horse as Cowboys rebuild both sides of the ball for 2026
articles.summary: America's Team added Von Miller and new defensive coordinator Christian Parker to fix a unit that allowed a league-worst 511 points last season.
articles.body: When a franchise carries the immense expectations of "America’s Team," back-to-back years without playoff runs can ignite immediate urgency across the entire organization. Few teams in the NFL have operated under as intense a microscope over the last few seasons as the Dallas Cowboys. With head coach Brian Schottenheimer entering his second year steering the ship, new defensive coordinator Christian Parker taking over, and Dak Prescott under center, Dallas is aiming to prove that last season’s sub-.500 stumble was a fluke and that their explosive roster can climb back into the NFC elite. Last Year The Cowboys experienced a bizarre, roller-coaster 2025 season, ultimately finishing 7-9-1 and failing to qualify for the postseason. At their best, the offense was a sheer powerhouse—Dak Prescott threw for 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns, ranking among the league's top passing leaders while feeding a dominant receiving corps. At their worst, the defense was somewhere between non-existent and awful. Dallas allowed a staggering 511 points (30.1 points per game), which finished dead last in the entire NFL. The disconnect between a top-10 scoring offense and the league’s worst defense led to a slew of shootout losses and cost defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus his job after just one season. QUINNEN WILLIAMS AGREES TO $105.9M CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH COWBOYS, LOCKING HIM IN THROUGH 2030 SEASON Offseason additions and subtractions Fixing the defensive disaster was the top priority from January through August. Dallas cleaned house on the defensive coaching staff, hiring 34-year-old defensive backs coach Christian Parker from Philadelphia as their new coordinator. To overhaul the roster, Jerry Jones and the front office prioritized bolstering the defense through both free agency and the draft. They selected top safety and pass-rush talent in the early rounds of the 2026 draft and signed veteran edge rusher Von Miller alongside defensive tackle Otito Ogbonnia and linebackers Chop Robinson and Kenneth Murray. They also re-signed star kicker Brandon Aubrey to a long-term deal and placed the franchise tag on wide receiver George Pickens to preserve a dynamic receiver tandem. On the subtraction side, Dallas parted ways with several depth pieces, including linebacker Logan Wilson (retired), safety Juanyeh Thomas, and edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney. Roster There is legitimate reason for optimism when looking at Dallas’ high-ceiling roster makeup. Offensively, the unit features one of the most explosive wide receiver duos in football, pairing CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. With Javonte Williams leading the backfield and a solid offensive line giving Prescott time in the pocket, Dallas has all the firepower needed to rank near the top of the league in total yardage and points once again. PRIVATE MAN WITH A PUBLIC LIFE DAK PRESCOTT ADDRESSES BROKEN ENGAGEMENT PUBLICLY FOR THE FIRST TIME The true wildcard is the defense. Under Christian Parker, the unit shifts toward a more aggressive, Vic Fangio-inspired scheme designed to eliminate big plays. With key draft additions filling secondary gaps alongside veteran pass rushers upfront, even a middle-of-the-pack defensive performance would drastically change Dallas' game-to-game outlook. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES 2026 OUTLOOK: WHY BETTING ON THEM TO MISS THE PLAYOFFS HAS REAL VALUE Betting Outlook The books seem to think the Cowboys will be better as well, putting them at 9.5 wins for the year. I like the idea of the over on them and think that they will win the NFC East this season. I also think that Dak Prescott gets a bit more love, and I’ll take a shot on him to win the MVP this year. Things don’t always seem to go the way you’d want if you’re a Cowboys fan, but it does seem like this team finally has some balance on both sides of the ball. Their offensive line seems like it will be strong enough to give Prescott time to throw, and the defensive line should be improved. Give me the over 9.5 wins, the Cowboys to win the East, and Prescott for MVP. articles.title: NFL Reportedly to Continue 'Strict' Enforcement of Sportsmanship-Related Rules in 2026
articles.summary: Last year, the NFL announced that it would be cracking down on "unsportsmanlike" and "inappropriate" gestures.
articles.body:
Last year, the NFL announced that it would be cracking down on "unsportsmanlike" and "inappropriate" gestures.

This year, the league's "strict enforcement of sportsmanship-related rules" will continue, according to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.

"The NFL will continue to stress strict enforcement of its sportsmanship-related rules by its on-field officials this season," Maske wrote.

"That means the officials will be expected to keep a close eye on players violating the league's rules prohibiting taunting opponents, illegal celebrations and fighting, at the behest of the NFL's competition committee."

The NFL announced its emphasis on sportsmanship last August, with NFL officiating rules analyst Walt Anderson saying :

"Unsportsmanlike gestures like simulating or either shooting a gun or brandishing a gun, or inappropriate gestures like a throat slash, or unfortunate sexual gestures, those were up 133% so that is a point of emphasis," Anderson said.

"The officials have made it a point of emphasis to the clubs. It's just one of those areas that the league wants to work actively on. There are plenty of ways for players to be able to celebrate, and they come up with some very unique and often entertaining ways so we want them to focus on those and not the inappropriate areas."

NFL Executive Vice President of Football Operations Troy Vincent had this to say in a video sent to teams last April:

"There's no place in the game to be standing over your opponent," Vincent said. "There's no place in the game to have violent gestures. That's not the game of football. We just have to play by the rules, respect your opponent, respect your teammates and play the game in between the whistles."

The NFL's crackdown on gestures happened after a 2024 season where numerous players were getting fined for various celebrations, including Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London , Kansas City Chiefs wideout Xavier Worthy , Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes , Detroit Lions receiver Jameson Williams , New York Jets wide receiver Allen Lazard and more.

All told, there were 31 fines for obscene gestures totaling $364,327, per Spotrac . Those numbers went down a bit in 2025 (30 fines, $327,249).

It's clear the NFL is still on the lookout for such acts, as evidenced by Maske's report, so chances are we'll be seeing more fines in the future.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes is looking at the Chiefs’ difficult 6-11 season differently after his injury and why he calls it “part of the journey”
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is ready to look ahead as the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is nearing his return after tearing his ACL and MCL last December, an inj.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is ready to look ahead as the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback is nearing his return after tearing his ACL and MCL last December, an injury that ended his 2025 season. The Chiefs also missed the playoffs for the first time in a decade after going 6-11. Now, as Mahomes prepares for his 10th NFL season, he says the difficult year was simply another part of his story.Patrick Mahomes reflects on Chiefs’ difficult 2025 seasonSpeaking exclusively to PEOPLE, Mahomes said the time away from football gave him a chance to focus on parts of his life that can be harder to enjoy during a busy NFL season.“Football is a huge part of my life, but I’ve always tried to keep perspective,” Mahomes told PEOPLE. “Family, friends, my teammates, my foundation work, those things have always been important to me.”Mahomes spent months working through his recovery while also having more time with his wife, Brittany, and their three children. The quarterback said that slower pace helped him appreciate time with his family.“During the season you’re so locked in, so having that time to slow down, be present with the kids, and just enjoy the people around you makes it special,” he said.The injury also forced Mahomes to spend much of the offseason focused on rehab. ESPN reported that Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Mahomes was often spending about seven hours a day at the team facility working on his recovery.Still, Mahomes does not appear interested in dwelling on what went wrong last season. He described the experience in simple terms.“Every season adds something to your story, good or bad,” Mahomes told PEOPLE. “My focus is always on what’s next.”Patrick Mahomes looks ahead to Chiefs’ 2026 seasonThat mindset is now turning toward a new season. Mahomes said his goal is not only to play well but also to be someone his family, teammates and young fans can look up to.“I want to be the best for my family, my teammates, the kids who look up to this game,” he said.He also wants to make sure he leaves the game without regrets.“When I think about why I go out there and put in the work every single day, it’s about being the best version of myself every single day so that I can have no regrets for how I played this game and went about my business,” Mahomes said.The Chiefs have also made changes around him. Kenneth Walker III and Emmanuel Ogbah were among their offseason additions as Kansas City tries to move forward from last season.Mahomes knows the team cannot simply repeat what worked before. “What makes great teams work is knowing that every year is a different team and every guy brings something different to the table,” he said.Kansas City is scheduled to open the 2026 regular season at home against the Denver Broncos on Sept. 14.
